#757. Quentin Tarantino and Wife Daniella Pick Welcome Baby No. 3

Quentin Tarantino and his wife Daniella Pick shared that they have welcomed their third baby together, a boy, with the new addition joining their kids Leo, 6, and Ariana, 4.

Once upon a time… Quentin Tarantino became a father of three.

Four years after the birth of their second child, the Oscar winner and his wife Daniella Pick Tarantino welcomed their third baby, Quentin’s rep confirmed to People Nov. 22.

“Quentin Tarantino and his wife, Daniella Pick Tarantino, are overjoyed to announce the birth of their third child,” the rep said in a statement to the outlet, “a baby boy.”

The couple—who tied the knot in 2018—also share son Leo, 6, and daughter Ariana, 4.

And while Quentin, 63, has kept his family life rather private, he has described fatherhood as an emotional experience.

“I can’t even see his name written on a piece of paper without crying,” the Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood filmmaker told CBS This Morning in July 2021, referring to Leo, whom he praised as the “most charming human being I’ve ever met in my life.”

“Half the time, I look at him and I’m just laughing because he’s so funny,” he continued. “And the other time, I’m just bursting into tears.”

And though Quentin’s first born shares a first name with one of his frequent collaborators Leonardo DiCaprio, he and his wife didn’t choose the moniker because of the Titanic star.

“We almost didn't name him [Leo] because people would assume that I named him after Leonardo DiCaprio,” Quentin shared during a June 2021 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live. “There's nothing wrong with that but I didn't.”

“He's named after my wife's grandfather,” Quentin said, “but also because, just in our hearts, he was our little lion.”

And for the Pulp Fiction director—who splits his time between Los Angeles and his wife’s native Tel Avi, Israel—fatherhood has been his top priority.

After all, Quentin revealed last year that he was delaying his tenth and final film to focus on his family.

“The idea of jumping on a voyage when they’re too young to understand it is not enticing to me," the Hateful Eight filmmaker said of his kids at the 2025 Sundance Film Festival, per People. “I want to not do whatever movie I end up doing until my son is at least 6. That way he’ll know what’s going on, he’ll be there, and it will be a memory for the rest of his life.”

As Quentin and Daniella’s brood enjoy their new normal as a family of five, keep reading for more stars who welcomed babies this year…

The Big Bang Theory alum gave birth to her second baby, a girl named Philomena Carmine Bobby Pelphrey, with the Task actor on Oct. 12.

"There are no words to describe this feeling once again. What a blessing," Cuoco—who's also mom to daughter Matilda—shared on instagram. "We are so grateful for the crazy wild up and down journey that brought us to our little Philo! Family officially complete."

The "No Problem" rapper confirmed that he and his partner welcomed a baby girl, Hayli, in November 2026.

Welcome to the world Hayli," Chance—dad to two older kids with ex Kirsten Corley—wrote in an Instagram post. "Mom n Dad love you. God is with you."

The Indianapolis Colts cornerback and his fiancée Monique Cook shared that they welcomed their third baby, a boy named Chosen Mani Ward, on Sept. 28.

The two are already parents to son Charvarius Ward Jr. as well as daughter Amani Joy, who died in 2024 at 23 months.

The Grey's Anatomy alum confirmed the arrival of his baby with the Spanish actress in a hilarious video recreating Spike Lee's 1989 movie Do The Right Thing.

Life got sweeter for the Disney Channel alum and the Victoria's Secret model after she gave birth to their first child—a baby girl—in early September.

Hinting at their daughter's birth date, the couple wrote on Instagram, "We took Labor Day literally this year."

Hold on tight, spider monkey—because the Twilight alum and his wife welcomed their first baby together on Sept. 16.

And yes, the couple did make a reference to their identical names when choosing a moniker for their new daughter Lennon Taylor Lautner.

Over one year after adopting their daughter, the Stranger Things star and the Sweethearts actor added a baby boy to their family, writing on Instagram in September 2026, "hi little guy!"

The Girls actress shared on Sept. 16 that the pair welcomed their first child, a daughter, via surrogate.

“Hello. I’m your mama," she recalled telling her baby in a Vogue essay. "You … you look nothing like I thought you would, but exactly right. We’ve been waiting for you, do you know that? It was so nice of you to come.”

On Sept. 11, multiple outlets reported that the "Born This Way" singer and her fiancé of over two years had welcomed their first baby together.

A birth certificate obtained by E! News later revealed that their child—a girl named Rose Bean Polansky—was born on June 9 in Los Angeles.

You can count on the Duggars to expand their brood. The 19 Kids & Counting alum and his wife announced the arrival of their fourth baby on Aug. 7, writing on Instagram, "Life feels busier than ever, yet we find ourselves trying to slow down to just soak in these days with our littles. And we wouldn’t have it any other way!"

John Lennon and Yoko Ono's son announced that he and his partner welcomed a baby boy in a Sept. 1 social media post.

"Okay so…Charlotte and I would like to announce that [we] have indeed created a Human Bean!"  Ono Lennon wrote. "His name is, Aurelius! Thank you!"

The Real Housewives of New Jersey alum Caroline Manzo's son welcomed his second child with his wife, who captioned photos of their newborn baby boy on Aug. 4, "Welcome to the world our sweet Theodore."

The youngest daughter of Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson gave birth to her third child—a baby girl—on Aug. 3 at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal.

"The baby was born weighing 6 pounds 9 ounces,"  a statement read on the royal family’s official Instagram page, adding that King Charles III and Queen Camilla "were delighted to be informed of the news.”

The Challenge alums announced that they had welcomed their fifth baby together Aug. 2, less than a year after having their daughter Francesca.

"With a 2-week early grand entrance, we'd like to welcome Vincent John into the world," Compono wrote on Instagram Aug. 3. "What originally was a checkup due to cramping led to a medically necessary induction due to low fluid (Oligo). Love you to bunches, my little Vinny boy."

The Marvel star and the Peaky Blinders actress welcomed their first baby together in July 2026, mulitple outlets reported.

The "I Need to Know" singer became a dad of eight when his wife gave birth to their daughter Myla, sharing in a July 21 that their family is "over the moon."

“What a great blessing to be able to share with you the arrival of our precious MYLA,” the couple wrote in a joint statement. “You can't imagine the happiness we have at home."

On an episode of her LadyGang podcast, the Glee alum announced that her seond baby—a daughter named Meyer June Martin—"decided to make an early entrance into the world."

"She was supposed to be born August 26, and she was born July 19," Tobin revealed, explaining how her surrogate had to induce labor due to preeclampsia. "The doctor was like, 'You know what? At this point, the baby is cooked pretty nicely.'"

This is...a family of five. After announcing their pregnancy in January, the couple confirmed the arrival of their baby boy in July.

"These last couple of weeks have been chaos, but in the best possible way," Mariano wrote in an Instagram post. "Welcome back home Rock-Anthony Makoa Ventimiglia. Can’t wait for all of the adventures ahead with our family of 5!"

The couple—who have been dating since at least 2023—confirmed they welcomed a baby together, with the actor jokingly telling E! News at the premiere of The Hawk, "It's nice to be out before I go back to work on my shift."

The couple announced they'd welcomed their baby on July 1 after Campbell's water broke early.

"Feels like heaven on earth,” she captioned a July 1 video of her cradling the newborn. "Baby is here and healthy.”

Zack Goytowski & Bliss Poureetezadi-Goytowski

Love is unique—just ask the parents of baby boy Polaris J ³ ohn Pax Goytowski.

Yes, the Love Is Blind couple gave their son what they described as a "three-dimensional name represented in two-dimensional space" when he was born on June 29.

The reveal of the unconventional moniker—an homage to three J-named family members—comes two years after the birth of their daughter Galileo Terri Rayne Goytowski.

The When Calls the Heart costars confirmed that they welcomed a baby girl in April, 10 months after they secretly wed in June 2025.

"Our daughter has been the greatest gift,” they told People in an interview published June 23, “and we are loving getting to know her better with each passing day."

The Summer House alum and her boyfriend welcomed their first baby together, Aidan Santos Heavey, on June 21, 10 weeks earlier than expected.

"He's heading to summer camp at NICU for the first 2/3 months in this world, but mom and dad can't wait to bring him home hopefully soon," Heavey wrote on Instagram. "Dad was a nervous, terrified, sobbing mess but couldn't ask for a better first Father's Day."

On June 11, the Dancing With the Stars alum announced she had given birth to her third child, a son named Hayes Duff Cusick, with her husband of 10 years.

"Baby boy is here," she captioned Instagram photos of herself holding the newborn in the hospital after her C-section, "and we are so grateful and so in love."

The Days of Our Lives alum and his wife welcomed their second baby together—a boy named Sebastian Antonio Barash—on June 5.

"House is full," Barash—who also shares son Joaquin with Devoto and daughter Harper with ex-wife Kirsten Storms—wrote on Instagram. "Hearts fuller."

A baby has entered the villa! The Love Island UK couple announced on June 4 that they had welcomed their second baby together—a boy.

The Pentatonix member and his husband welcomed a baby girl named Birde James Hoying via surrogate on June 3.

"The process of us having a child took four or five years," Hoying told People in an interview published June 23. "It's been a long time coming and just looking at her, I started crying because it was just such a beautiful thing that I feel really, really lucky."

The "Big Mama" rapper welcomed her first baby, a girl, with the "Bank Account" artist.

"There were tears and anxiety was through the roof," she noted about her pregnancy in an Apple Music interview published May 29. "It's what I wanted but I was just like, 'Wait, this real life, like am I really ready?' But ultimately, obviously had her and I'm glad I made the decision to do it."

The influencer and DJ welcomed baby girl Juliette July Fedyk on June 1, sharing that she was born early at 33 weeks.

"Suddenly the world just got a whole lot brighter," Madeleine posted to Instagram June 2. "06.01.2026 4lbs and 17.2 inches. We love you so much and are so proud to be your parents x."

The Laguna Beach alum and the NASCAR reporter announced the arrival of their first baby, Rhodes August Colletti, on Instagram May 14.

#754. COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels

The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

The goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is important because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The new negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," said Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible."

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

"For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," said Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry."

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but said it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs."

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she said in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

"Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," said Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance."

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," said Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

At 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

"The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," said Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030."

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

"The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have said to me that they want to help get an outcome."

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, said the draft text showed a level of "seriousness" on important issues like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

"The question is whether the level of ambition on those issues is carried through into the final outcome here," said Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days."

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

Update, November 17, 2026: This article has been updated with additional reactions to the draft text.

#753. Taylor Swift Celebrates Travis Kelce’s Touchdowns With Niece Wyatt

Taylor Swift and her niece Wyatt Kelce cheered on Travis Kelce as he scored two historic touchdowns for his career during the Kansas City Chiefs’ Nov. 22 game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Prepare for a few teardrops on your guitar after seeing Taylor Swift’s sweet moment with her niece Wyatt.

The Grammy winner proved she’s just a girl who’s found a place in this world as an auntie as she and the 7-year-old cheered on her husband Travis Kelce during his Kansas City Chiefs’ Nov. 22 face-off against the Arizona Cardinals.

During the matchup at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City—which marked Travis’ 100th regular season home game—the NFL star scored not one, but two career-defining touchdowns while dominating the field. In the game’s first quarter, his touchdown launched him into third place all-time for the most career touchdowns by an NFL tight end, which was followed by a second touchdown that marked his first two-touchdown game since 2022.

And it was clear that Taylor and Wyatt—the eldest daughter of the “Opalite” singer’s in-laws Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce’s four kids—were in a state of grace over the achievement as footage shared to social media Nov. 22 caught them in a sweet embrace after the second play.

The 36-year-old—donning a Chiefs windbreaker from Erin Andrews’ WEAR clothing line and her signature red lip—yelled in excitement from her suite as she hugged Wyatt from behind.

And it’s clear Wyatt was thrilled to have her aunt wrapped around her like a cardigan as she smiled wide.

But they weren’t the only ones enchanted by Travis’ skills on the field. After all, the athlete did a little celebrating himself after his 22-yard touchdown reception, yelling “come on!” as he jumped up and down.

The thrilling moment comes one week after Travis suffered an ankle injury that left him temporarily sidelined during his team's 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta Nov. 15.

Thankfully, the 37-year-old made it clear he was Mr. Perfectly Fine after the ordeal.

"I'm all good," Travis told USA Today after the game. "I probably could have went more than I did when I came back, but it was the direction the team wanted to go, so I was right there with them."

"We had a lot of young guys step up," he added, "so it was really nice."

It’s also always nice to see Taylor fulfill her auntie duties, which Travis recently admitted took his nieces a while to get used to.

“We had to break that habit of your daughters,” Travis said on the Sept. 16 episode of his and Jason’s New Heights podcast. “When they got to meet Aunt Tay Tay, they were calling her 'Taylor Swift.’”

In fact, Jason—who also shares daughters Elliotte, 5, Bennett, 3, and Finnley, 20, months with Kylie—recalled them saying, “‘Taylor Swift, can I do this? Taylor Swift!’”

And while they seem to be more comfortable with Taylor’s big reputation these days, Kylie shared that her little ones wanted the “Cardigan” singer to be a part of the family even before she wed their Uncle Trav this past July.

"They’re so excited they’re getting another aunt, and we could not be more excited for them and what the future holds," the Not Gonna Lie podcast host added on Good Morning America last September. "We love love, and we love Taylor and Trav."

Keep reading for all the reasons sparks continue to fly for Taylor and Travis…

Long before Taylor Swift's attendance at the Kansas City Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 game became one of the definitive pop culture moments of the year, Travis Kelce was an admirer of the Grammy winner.

The star tight end's interest in Taylor was first revealed by one of his teammates in a TikTok video posted by the Chiefs in August 2023 (which, in hindsight, was when the pair were secretly dating).

Before Travis could answer the prompt of who his celebrity crush was, wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling spilled, "Taylor Swift!"

Travis smiled at the camera before holding his finger up to his mustache, saying, "Alright now!"

Plus, Travis was just one of many celebs to attend Taylor's record-breaking Eras Tour even before the now-engaged duo kicked off their romance. But more on that enchanting moment in a bit...

No. 2: He's Not Her Usual Type (on Paper)

While he does have that daydream look in his eyes (especially when he sees Taylor on the big-screen at one of his games), Travis stands out a bit when you look back at Taylor’s dating history.

She is typically attracted to creative types, including actors (Joe Alwyn, Jake Gyllenhaal, Taylor Lautner and Tom Hiddleston) and musicians (Calvin Harris, John Mayer, Harry Styles and, most recently, Matty Healy).

But perhaps that’s why her romance with the lighthearted and cheeky athlete—who signed an updated two-year deal with the Chiefs worth $34.25 million in 2024—feels like such a refreshing option for Taylor after her six-year uber-private relationship with Joe came to an end in April 2023.

Looks like the 10-time Pro Bowler’s wishes came true after he all but manifested his romance with the superstar through sheer will, determination and declarations of infatuation.

Travis publicly aired his failed attempt to shoot his shot and talk to Taylor when he attended the Kansas City stop on her Eras Tour July 7, 2023. As it turns out, he had a special gift for her: A friendship bracelet bearing his "number" that he hoped to give Taylor. (He wouldn't definitively say if it was his jersey number or phone number.)

Despite his claim that he was "disappointed" he failed to meet her after the concert, Taylor confirmed to TIME in December 2023 that she belatedly caught his podcast pass.

"Travis very adorably put me on blast on his podcast, which I thought was metal as hell," she recalled. "We started hanging out right after that. So we actually had a significant amount of time that no one knew, which I'm grateful for, because we got to get to know each other."

So, that whole theory about the Sept. 24 game being their first official hang? As Taylor clarified to TIME, "We would never be psychotic enough to hard launch a first date."

Since dating Travis, Taylor has been seen in public more frequently, including outings with friends in NYC and jubilant appearances at award shows, like the 2023 MTV VMAs and the 2024 Grammys.

But her most talked-about appearance? Sitting in Travis' suite at the Chief's Sept. 24, 2023 home game against the Chicago Bears.

Rather than shy away from the attention, Taylor cheered and screamed "Let's f--king go!" when Travis scored a touchdown. Like the public, even Travis admitted he was caught off-guard by Taylor accepting his invite.

"Shoutout to Taylor for pulling up, that was pretty ballsy," Travis said days later on his New Heights podcast. "I just thought it was awesome how everyone in the suite had nothing but great things to say about her, the friends and family."

"She looked amazing," he added. " It was definitely a game I will remember, that's for damn sure."

Since then, Taylor and Travis have been photographed hand-in-hand on dates all around the world and have made multiple visits to a Christmas bar in Kansas City, where they were not shy about PDA.

And, after revealing to TIME that she retreated from the spotlight when Kim Kardashian's infamous leaked phone call in 2016, Taylor is going out tonight...and every night, if she wants to, thank you very much.

"Life is short," she said. "Have adventures. Me locking myself away in my house for a lot of years—I’ll never get that time back. I’m more trusting now than I was six years ago.”

While Travis isn't afraid to spill some tea on his Sept. 27, 2023 podcast regarding his interactions with Taylor, he still expressed his boundaries about addressing his personal life moving forward.

"I know I brought all this attention to me," he explained. "I did the whole friendship bracelet thing and told everyone how butthurt I was that I didn't get to meet Taylor." However, he continued, he didn't plan to give a full play-by-play of their relationship.

"What's real is that it is my personal life and I want to respect both of our lives," he explained. "I'm enjoying life and I sure as hell enjoyed this weekend. So everything moving forward, I think me talking about sports and saying 'alright nah' will have to be where I keep it."

He doubled-down on his desire to play it cool in a November 2023 interview with the Wall Street Journal.

"Everybody around me telling me: Don't f--k this up! And me sitting here saying: Yeah—got it," he told the outlet, before addressing the media attention. "That was the biggest thing to me: make sure I don't say anything that would push Taylor away."

But that doesn't mean he's been able to resist publicly talking about his girlfriend—crediting her for the boost in sales of his jersey and calling her "amazing" after she was booed by New England Patriots fans at a December 2023 game.

"I've never been a man of words," he admitted to WSJ. "Being around her, seeing how smart Taylor is, has been f--king mind-blowing. I'm learning every day."

Like Taylor, who is close with her parents, particularly her mother Andrea, Travis hails from a tight-knit fam, including his parents Ed and Donna Kelce.

Donna became a beloved public figure as the first mother to have two sons playing against each other in a Super Bowl, when Travis faced off against his older brother, Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, in the big game in February 2023.

"For all the stars to align and for them to get through high school and college and the pros. And for them to both play in the Pro Bowl and to play in the Super Bowl, and then for this to happen," Donna told ET at the time. "This is just like a dream come true. I can't express enough how special this is for the family and it's just crazy."

Donna, who was married to Ed for 25 years before they divorced, supported both of her sons by wearing a half-black, half-red Eagles and Chiefs jacket.

After the Super Bowl, which saw the Chiefs best the Eagles, Travis and Jason got emotional while reflecting on sharing the experience with Donna.

"The moment I saw mom is when I got really emotional," Jason said on the brothers' New Heights podcast. "It was so awesome...She was on top of the world for a week."

"She was the heavyweight champ man," Travis added. "She was on top of it, and she shined the whole time."

Like Taylor and her younger brother Austin Swift, Travis has a special bond with his older brother Jason, who inspired him to play football.

In addition to their impressive careers as NFL players, Travis and Jason launched their podcast New Heights in September 2022, a project that has only strengthened their relationship (and their bank accounts).

"What this did was gave us a scheduled two to three hour window where we have to talk to each other and we have to talk about what we're going through, throughout the week and throughout the games," Travis told NBC Sports in February 2023. "It's almost been like therapy, man."

Sure, the pair technically never met until 2023, but there have been a few invisible strings tying them together.

Taylor and Travis both count Miles Teller as a friend, with the Top Gun: Maverick star and his wife Keleigh Sperry even being recruited by Taylor to star in the music video for "I Bet You Think About Me" off Red (Taylor's Version) in 2021.

Travis, meanwhile, joined Miles and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes for golfing practice ahead of the American Century Championship in 2022.

Miles tweeted a photo of himself on the golf course with the athletes, writing, "Grip it and rip it." Travis proved the bromance was real when he reposted the shot and added, "Back at it like we never left!!"

(Interestingly enough, Miles is a noted diehard Philadelphia Eagles fans, so perhaps he put in a word with Jason to broker an IRL meet-up between Travis and Taylor?)

While Taylor attended the Sept. 24, 2023 game solo, she brought an entourage of celebrity friends with her when she attended the Chiefs' match-up against the New York Jets at New Jersey's Metlife Stadium on Oct. 1.

She was accompanied by BFFs Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds and his friend Hugh Jackman, as well as Sophie Turner, Sabrina Carpenter and Queer Eye's Antoni Porowski.

While their attendance at the game spoke volumes, even more telling was Ryan following Travis on Instagram.

Not only has Travis played in four Super Bowls, winning three of them (NBD!), but he's also hosted Saturday Night Live, so you know he can handle intense spotlight with ease.

That may seem trivial, but Taylor has penned several songs regarding her fear that her level of fame could prove to be too much for her romantic partner to handle. (See: "Peace" and "The Archer.")

"It all depends who you're with," Taylor said in, "If they have a serious issue with it, I guess you'll hide or whatever, but I don't really like that, because it makes me feel like I'm running from the law or something. I don't want to feel like a fugitive, like, 'Oh my god, we're having a relationship, better hide!'

"I feel like if you can be in a relationship and have it seem normal, that would be good."

And in his WSJ interview, Travis proved he's more than ready for the pressure that comes with being married to someone as powerful as Taylor.

"Obviously I've never dated anyone with that kind of aura about them...I've never dealt with it," he said. "But at the same time, I'm not running away from any of it."

"The scrutiny she gets, how much she has a magnifying glass on her, every single day, paparazzi outside her house, outside every restaurant she goes to, after every flight she gets off, and she's just living, enjoying life," he added. "When she acts like that I better not be the one acting all strange."

Further proving their love is worthy of a rom-com treatment, fans were swooning after a concertgoer captured video of Taylor running into Travis' arms and exchanging a passionate kiss after performing in Argentina in November 2023. And that was after she changed the lyrics in Karma from "the guy on the screen" to "the guy on the Chiefs," much to Travis' surprise as he attended alongside her father, Scott Swift.

Turning out for one another's stadium takeovers—Taylor attended 13 Chiefs games her first season with Travis, traveling straight from her Tokyo show to make the Super Bowl—is a show of how serious their relationship is.

"I'm going to see him do what he loves, we're showing up for each other, other people are there and we don't care," Taylor told TIME of their public support. "The opposite of that is you have to go to an extreme amount of effort to make sure no one knows that you're seeing someone. And we're just proud of each other."

And if her presence at the NFL games annoys you, well, Taylor can't even be bothered to have bad blood with you.

"There's a camera, like, a half-mile away, and you don't know where it is, and you have no idea when the camera is putting you in the broadcast, so I don't know if I'm being shown 17 times or once," she said. "I'm just there to support Travis. I have no awareness of if I'm being shown too much and pissing off a few dads, Brads, and Chads."

Travis was born in—are you ready for it?—1989. Screaming, crying, throwing up, etc.

Speaking of Killa Trav's birthday, which falls on October 5, did you know he shares his with Taylor's late grandmother Marjorie Finlay, the subject of her song "Marjorie" off of 2020's evermore? If we didn't know better, we'd think this is a sign...

She's loved him three summers now, honey, and she's going to get 'em all.

#752. PSG's Doue to have surgery on ruptured ACL

Desire Doue has scored six goals in all competitions for PSG this season

Paris St-Germain forward Desire Doue will have surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.

The 21-year-old was in tears as he was taken off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half in the Ligue 1 champions' 3-2 victory over Nice on Saturday night.

Doue, who has arguably been PSG's best player this season, twisted awkwardly and went down under no contact.

The match was stopped for five minutes as Doue - who was visibly in pain - received treatment before he was applauded off by the crowd at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.

It is a huge set-back for the France attacker, who missed 13 games in 2025-26 with calf and hamstring injuries.

The European champions have been plagued with injury issues so far this season and are already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who sustained an ACL injury of his own against Barcelona in October.

PSG return to action on Wednesday, when they host Roma in the Champions League.

#751. 'Rolls-Royce' Iqbal's 'dream' journey from Old Trafford to Tannadice

Jim Goodwin's side are eight games unbeaten, with Zidane Iqbal pivotal

Given the superlatives being thrown in the direction of Zidane Iqbal by the Scottish football fraternity, one would think he was a replica of a certain France great instead of just sharing his name.

So much so that BBC Radio Scotland pundits were suggesting on Saturday's Sportsound that the 23-year-old is the answer to Celtic's hunt for a long-term successor to captain Callum McGregor as their midfield general.

It is just as well for Dundee United that the Iraq international is tied to them until at least the summer, his early season appearances for Utrecht ruling out a transfer during the January window.

So, where has he sprung from and what is all the fuss about?

Hibs 0-4 Dundee United: What Goodwin said

Born in Manchester to a Pakistani father and an Iraqi mother, Iqbal came through the Old Trafford youth system.

He signed his first professional contract with United in 2021 and became the first British-born South Asian and first-ever British South Asian to play in the Champions League when he came on as an 89th-minute substitute against Young Boys that December.

However, that was to be his one and only first-team appearance and, although he had already made his international debut in a World Cup qualifier at the age of 19, he was sold to Utrecht for a reported fee of Â£1m in summer 2023.

Starting off in their Jong Utrecht second string, he would go on to make 49 appearances for the Dutch top-flight outfit before making a surprise switch to the Scottish Premiership this summer.

On the one hand, United were getting a player who played all three of Iraq's games at this summer's World Cup, two of them starts, albeit all three were heavy defeats.

On the other hand, Iqbal had only managed seven appearances last season for Utrecht and had been a second-half substitute in two of their four matches at the start of the new campaign.

However, after a pivotal display in what was being described as a midfield "masterclass" by United in Saturday's 4-0 dismantling of hosts Hibernian, manager Jim Goodwin revealed he always had belief the Tangerines were unearthing a "Rolls-Royce".

"The head of recruitment's job is to go and identify good talent for us," Goodwin told BBC Scotland. "It's my job to give him the profile and then he goes out and does the groundwork.

"We could see immediately when we watched the footage of Zidane and when we had the Zoom call with him and his representatives, we not only had a fantastic player but a really good person with the right characteristics to come and fit the culture here."

Zidane Iqbal was also a marked man at the World Cup finals

While on-loan Rangers man Lyall Cameron was among the goals and fellow 24-year-old Dylan Tait provided a stylish assist, it was the third leg of what some regard as the best midfield triumvirate in the Premiership who was singled out for most praise at Easter Road.

With former Celtic winger Aidan McGeady again pondering the question about McGregor's likely successor, transfer market expert and former United wing-back Allan Preston opined: "A six for Celtic? Look no further than young Iqbal.

"He's been magnificent since he's come to Scottish football, absolutely brilliant. Running the show again.

"If Celtic are looking for a young boy at his age with experience, he is a full international, knows the game, played in Scotland, you can see what he can do, there's your man in front of you.

"Other players' hair's on fire, but he's just nice and calm. He's at a different level. He doesn't panic. When the ball comes to him, he is so calm on it, he takes his time, he's got great peripheral vision."

The former Dundee United wing-back pointed out, though: "He's had his two clubs that he can play for in a year of football, so he is going nowhere until at least the summer, so enjoy him while you can because I think you'll get serious money for this young boy."

McGeady pointed to Iqbal's "good pedigree", having started with Manchester United and already having 32 caps for Iraq, but wondered if that would be enough for Celtic to consider him.

"I don't even think, if he's performing this well, Celtic will go and get him," said McGeady.

"Why are Celtic not looking at players like this? Do they feel they have to prove themselves somewhere else first?"

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown was similarly impressed.

"He's been a delight to watch - sharpness to get on the ball and willingness to drive forward," the former midfielder and manager pointed out.

"He beats a man in the middle of the park as well and there's not too many midfielders willing to do that.

"Watching him there talking to the media, he can't get the smile off his face. He enjoys football, he takes the ball under pressure, he does things that other people don't do, especially in midfield.

"He brings composure, but he can also drive through as well. His willingness to keep getting on the ball, even if he makes that slight mistake - that's what I really enjoy watching about him."

While Goodwin reckons there will be likely interest in the summer, Iqbal has no thoughts of so quickly leaving a club - and manager - who have resurrected his club career.

"I'm not even looking at any other clubs," he told BBC Scotland. "I'm fully focused on Dundee United.

"They've given me a platform to enjoy myself and play football. I'm really enjoying my football again.

"They've given me faith and confidence. The gaffer and the coaching staff have a lot of belief in me.

"The bare minimum I can do is pay them back with strong performances and hopefully it carries on."

Iqbal recalled being at Manchester United's "development centre since I was four or five - I signed when I was eight", explaining that he "then left for some first-team football".

He stressed that his lack of games last season came as a result of "a couple of injuries" and, while "I learnt a lot in Holland", he is "happy to have left that behind me", adding: "That book's closed now."

Visit our Dundee United page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Get Dundee United news notifications in the BBC Sport app

Iqbal also recalled how Goodwin's enthusiasm persuaded him to make the switch to Tannadice on deadline day.

"After the World Cup, I had one year left on my contract and I was in touch with my agent," the midfielder said. "We both wanted a move and I had a few chats with a few clubs.

"To be fair, I left it a bit late for Dundee United, but after the first call with the gaffer, I straight away called my agent after we ended the call.

"I said, 'look, I genuinely feel like the guy really believes in me'.

"It happened very late. I had to drive from Holland to Scotland. It was a tough drive but worth it in the end."

That World Cup was also a defining experience, with representing his country in the United States described as surreal.

"Having your friends and family there to watch you and playing on the world stage, with so many people, was a dream," he said.

"Playing against top players gave me that confidence boost I needed. I thought I did well in the three tough games.

"I knew, wherever I'd end up, with the faith of the gaffer, I could really kick on and push because I've learnt so much from the World Cup."

Goodwin is the manager to have done that and Iqbal added: "He's such a top guy, not just in football.

"His tactics are amazing. Everyone's comfortable. Everyone wants to fight for him."

#750. Sandra Bullock Shares Rare Photos of Kids During Disneyland Trip

Sandra Bullock shared an inside look at a family trip to Disneyland with her kids Louis, 16, and Laila, 13: “Remind yourself of what it feels like to be a kid.”

Sandra Bullock is making sweet memories with her family.

The Practical Magic star shared a rare look at a magical outing with her kids Louis, 16, and Laila, 13, to Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, Calif., with Bullock posting photos and videos of her family enjoying amusement park rides, treats and holiday fun.

“Sometimes you just need to stop worrying and remind yourself of what it feels like to be a kid,” the Oscar winner wrote in a Nov. 22 Instagram post. “FYI There are no calories in ice cream if you ride the Guardians of the Galaxy ride and don’t cry.”

For the pixie-perfect day at Disneyland Park and Disneyland California Adventure, Bullock was joined by longtime pal Josh Holloway, his wife Yessica Holloway and their son Hunter, 12.

Tagging the couple in her post, the 62-year-old wrote “family and friends,” adding a heart emoji.

But the Proposal actress proved that her kids were at the front of her mind. After all, the first shot in the carousel featured the teens walking down Hollywood Boulevard in California Adventure.

And it’s safe to say Bullock and her loved ones were having a blast at the Happiest Place on Earth as she shared pics and videos of the group riding Radiator Springs Racers, Guardians of the Galaxy—Mission BREAKOUT! and Space Mountain.

The Blind Side actress also included an epic shot of her riding the rollercoaster with her kids, with Laila looking over at her mom with a grin as they rode in the front of the rocket.

Another photo in the carousel featured Bullock taking a selfie of her group from behind as they walked in the theme park, with the Miss Congeniality star sporting a Disneyland baseball cap.

And since a trip to Disneyland isn’t complete without a tasty treat, Bullock also shared a pic with a delicious cup of ice cream.

With Thanksgiving on the horizon, the Speed actress is feeling grateful.

Resharing photos from her post on her Instagram Stories, Bullock wrote, “Things I’m thankful for: family,” adding in follow-up slides that she's also thankful for “friends,” “life,” “ice cream” and ultimately, “EVERYTHING.”

#749. Pepe did not injure eyes staring at sun, say Villarreal

Nicolas Pepe (right) wore an eye mask on his return to the side following his eye operation in October

Villarreal say reports striker Nicolas Pepe needed eye surgery because he stared directly at the solar eclipse are "completely false".

In a statement, the Spanish club said an operation in October that ruled the 31-year-old out for six matches was "scheduled in advance" and "entirely unrelated" to the eclipse, which took place on 12 August.

Reports on social media suggested the former Arsenal forward had injured his eyes staring directly at the sun during the lunar event, with a video then emerging - purportedly from one of Pepe's social media accounts - showing him watching it in Spain.

"Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe's eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse," said the club.

"The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

"The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players' health."

Staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.

In the build-up to this summer's event, experts warned only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.

Ivory Coast international Pepe has scored 14 goals in 86 appearances in all competitions for Villarreal after joining from Trabzonspor in 2024.

He cost Arsenal a then-club record Â£72m when he joined from Lille in the summer of 2019.

Pepe scored 27 goals in 112 games for the Gunners and had a loan spell at Nice before joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

#748. Will Smith, Jada Pinkett Smith Step Out For Rare Family Outing

Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith enjoyed a multi-generational family outing with their kids Jaden, 28, and Willow, 26, and their moms Adrienne Banfield-Norris and Caroline Bright in Malibu.

Now this is a story all about how the Smith family had a special day out.

Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith enjoyed a rare public outing with their kids Jaden Smith, 28, and Willow Smith, 26, as they stepped out to visit Soho House’s Little Beach House Malibu in Malibu, Calif., on Nov. 21.

And it was a multi-generational family affair, with Will and Jada’s moms Caroline Bright and Adrienne Banfield-Norris, respectively, also tagging along for the outing at the oceanfront social club.

While the occasion appeared casual, the Smith brood didn’t slack on the fashion, with the family all making a statement with their looks.

Will, 58, sported a bright red zip-up, white T-shirt and jeans, which he accessorized with a white baseball hat. Jada, 55, meanwhile, rocked a chic black button-up shirt under a black leather jacket, along with dark grey trousers. The Girls Trip actress paired the look with red shoes and a black handbag.

As for the former couple’s kids, Willow donned a long green patterned coat over a pair of beige pants and boots, while Jaden kept it classic with a white zip-up hoodie.

And the family matriarchs made sure to show who’s in charge as Adrienne, 73, wore a navy sweater over camouflage pants and Caroline, 89, rocked a black-and-white printed ensemble.

Though Will and Jada—who quietly separated in 2016—have maintained a rather low profile in recent years, they have stepped out on multiple occasions to publicly show their support for their kids.

In June, the pair were joined by Willow, Adrienne and Will’s son Trey—whom he shares with ex Sheree Zampino—for a joint appearance at Paris Fashion Week to attend Christian Louboutin’s Menswear Spring/Summer 2027 show. After all, Jaden is the brand’s men’s creative director.

During the trip to the fashion capital, the pair enjoyed a night out with Jaden, linking arms as they stepped out for dinner.

The Paris outing came five months after Will and Jada reunited to support Jaden when he debuted his first collection with Christian Louboutin at Paris Fashion Week in January.

Though it’s been over a decade since the Bad Boys actor and Red Table Talk alum separated, Jada—who publicly revealed the breakup in 2023—shared that she and Will don’t plan on filing for divorce in the future.

As she told NBC News in Oct. 2023, “I made a promise that there will never be a reason for us to get a divorce.”

For a look back at Will and Jada’s relationship over the years, keep reading…

Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith were all smiles at the Devil in a Blue Dress premiere in 1995.

Have you ever seen anything more '90s glam than this? The couple posed together in 1997, the year they got married.

Jada was styling more than just a trendy silver coat in this 1998 red carpet photo—she was also showing off her baby bump in a sleek black dress. The couple's son Jaden Smith was born on July 8, 1998.

During Jada's second pregnancy with daughter Willow Smith in 2000, Will couldn't help but to cradle the actress' baby belly at a celebrity boxing match in Los Angeles.

Hats off to the couple who never cease to show up on a red carpet in style. Here they were together at Hollywood's Kodak Theater in 2005.

Jada ignored the old superstition of never wearing to black to a wedding as she and Will headed to Katie Holmes and Tom Cruise's 2006 nuptials in Rome.

The kids were here in London with Will and Jada on the red carpet at The Karate Kid premiere in 2010.

Orange you glad to see this picture of Will and Jada together? The pair got cozy during an event in New York City in 2010.

Willow, Jaden, Will and Jada posed together in a family shot at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2012.

Jada dazzled in green as she and Will arrived at the 2016 Golden Globe Awards at the Beverly Hilton Hotel.

Everyone was all smiles for a family vacation after making a quick pit stop at the 2018 World Cup.

In 2020, the couple addressed Jada's alleged affair with August Alsina.

Admitting she and August had an "entanglement" while she and Will were separated, she explained, "It was a relationship. I was in a lot of pain and I was very broken. In the process of that relationship I definitely realized you can't find happiness outside of yourself. Luckily enough, you and I were also going through a process of healing in a much different manner."

During the 2022 Academy Awards, Will slapped host Chris Rock over a joke the comedian made about Jada's shaved head.

After the slap, Will resigned from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences and was banned from its events for 10 years. He also apologized to Chris, calling the slap "unacceptable" and noting "there is no part of me that thinks that was the right way to behave in that moment."

In October 2023, Jada revealed she and Will had been separated for seven years, including the six leading up to the 2022 Oscars.

"We're still figuring it out," Jada told People. "We've been doing some really heavy-duty work together. We just got deep love for each other and we are going to figure out what that looks like for us."

#747. Spurs 'a match for anyone' as win at Man City boosts European hopes

Spurs secure famous win as Man City falter again

Dreams of reaching the Women's Champions League may have seemed fanciful for Tottenham Hotspur when the season began.

The Women's Super League has an established big four, and big-spending London City Lionesses were the side making the most obvious play to disrupt that dominance.

But a hugely impressive and deserved win at Manchester City on Sunday afternoon proves Spurs are a team on the up, and the table shows they remain firmly in top-three contention.

Two late goals secured a 3-1 win at Joie Stadium, but this was no smash-and-grab job. Spurs were more dynamic than sluggish City, pressing them into submission.

They restricted their hosts' stellar attack to precious few chances and took the ones they created.

"When we are on our game, we can be a match for anyone," Spurs manager Martin Ho said in his post-match media conference.

"It gives us confidence - but it is just one game."

Man City beaten by Spurs and miss chance to go top of WSL

Victory kept Spurs, whose highest finish in the WSL is fifth, firmly in the mix this time.

They are fifth again, but just three points behind London City Lionesses who occupy the final European place as the league heads into a last international break of 2026.

Chelsea lead the way from Manchester City, with Manchester United one point ahead of Tottenham, who in turn sit handily clear of their sixth-placed north London rivals Arsenal.

The big four are therefore all present in the top six. London City are right there, too, and Spurs, with six wins from 11 games so far, are gamely pressing their own case.

What made Sunday's win and performance from Tottenham even more impressive is how dreadful their recent record against Manchester City had been.

Tottenham had lost six of their previous seven away matches against City in all competitions, averaging over four goals conceded per defeat.

Last season City won this fixture 5-2 with Khadija Shaw scoring a 13-minute hat-trick, the quickest in WSL history.

Shaw's early goal on Sunday, her 16th in league matches versus Spurs, could easily have started a landslide.

That was expected. City had won each of their past 17 WSL home games, including all 10 in 2026 â until Tottenham tore up the script.

The outcome means Manchester City, beaten at Chelsea in their previous outing, have suffered consecutive league losses for the first time since January 2025.

Spurs have rediscovered form after losing all three league games in October while conceding 14 goals

Tottenham's victory came down to Ho's brave tactics and his team's superb execution of them.

After going behind, they pressed City constantly, forcing errors and creating chances. That tenacity won them countless one-on-ones, with City unable or unwilling to play over the press.

After her goal, Shaw was rendered anonymous by the hard work and close marking of centre-backs Toko Koga and Amanda Nilden.

Down the right, Kirsty Hanson dominated Carlotta Wamser, could have been awarded a penalty and provided the low cross for Cathinka Tandberg's equaliser.

In midfield, Drew Spence pulled all the strings and covered the entire pitch. At 34, she is perhaps playing the best football of her career and deserved her assist for the winner. After Matilda Vinberg put Spurs in front, several players ran to celebrate with Spence.

"When you come into this, you wonder if it will go against you, but the players were outstanding," said Ho.

"We haven't won here in so long, so we know it will be a tough game, but I have belief in my team when we are on song. I thought we were outstanding - we worked every blade of grass."

Spurs are clearly capable of taking the game to anyone in the league and have now scored 28 WSL goals this season, with only Chelsea and London City having more.

In the second half they adapted to City sending on such fluid attacking threats as Mary Fowler, Kerstin Casperij and Beth Mead.

They lifted the gas from the press, applying it more sparingly, and were solid in defence.

It shows that Ho has learned painful lessons from the past - whether from Spurs' poor record against City, including two five-goal losses in 2025-26, or conceding six to Chelsea and London City back to back in October.

"We have maybe been naive at times and I own that, so we are more reserved," Ho said of his tactical approach. "It was managing that, and the players' communication was excellent."

City were limited to fleeting chances. Jade Rose blasting over after keeper Lize Kop parried a Lauren Hemp free-kick was as close as they came to a second goal, and those were their first shots after a 50-minute drought.

When Spurs got their late chances through the hard work of Vinberg, they could strike for three points.

Vinberg had quite the rollercoaster afternoon. She was initially named on the bench but was promoted to the starting XI 15 minutes before kick-off as Olivia Holdt was suffering stomach cramps.

Perhaps unprepared, she gave away the ball playing out of defence leading to City's opener. But she grew into the game, scored Spurs' second goal and set up Jess Naz for the third.

It was a great moment for Naz, on her 100th WSL appearance of a career that has been disrupted by injury.

Spurs are back in Manchester before Christmas, visiting United on 20 December.

There will be real hope of a positive result as they press their way into contention for what would be a historic achievement of a top-three finish.

#746. Are Man Utd genuinely in a relegation battle?

After Manchester United's 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino's side officially have the worst defence in Europe and have endured their worst start to a season in over half a century - so are they going down?

Football Journalist @Ronnabe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

What started as a blip has become a problem far more systemic for Man Utd.

"If the name wasn't Man Utd and you're watching their performances, you'd say they are a team in a relegation fight. They're conceding lots of goals, a comedy of errors, red cards - they've won one game all season," said Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher.

Only Ipswich beaten in 11 attempts, the worst defence in Europe - and a 4-0 hammering at Liverpool on Sunday to wipe the gloss off Mauricio Pochettino's arrival within 12 first-half minutes.

Carragher added: "This Manchester United back four can't cope with pace. They're a million miles off it in terms of coming up against what they are in the Premier League."

The unthinkable is beginning to become thinkable. Are United in an actual relegation battle now?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"They're in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table," said Carragher after a fifth defeat of the season left them with their lowest points tally at this stage of a season since 1972. "You can't say anything else when you look at their record this season.

"We don't believe it will happen over a 38-game season, but they haven't had the most difficult of starts. They've played a lot of promoted teams; they haven't played the best team in the league, Arsenal, yet.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"I don't think they'll go down, but this idea that they haven't got a scrap on their hands, they have."

It seems unfathomable. But should it? The numbers don't give Pochettino any grounds for optimism. Only 26 teams - barely one a season - have picked up eight points or fewer from their opening 11 games in the history of the Premier League and only 13 of those, exactly half, avoided the drop.

Of course, most of those were not clubs anywhere near the size and stature of Manchester United. But even the Opta supercomputer, which provides far more contextualised feedback, is losing faith and gives them a 24 per cent chance of going down - though it does still back them to stumble to safety and finish 16th.

"You wonder how low it can get," said Gary Neville after Sunday's defeat. "It's embarrassing. I don't believe they're in a relegation fight, they'll get out of this, but this is the worst Man Utd have been in 53 years. The worst defensive team in Europe, second-bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options aren't great."

That may be putting it lightly. As well as the worst defence in Europe's top-five leagues across all competitions, United also have the third-worst performing attack in the Premier League, falling below their xG tally by 4.2 goals already.

In an immediately infamous tweet in 2014, then-boss David Moyes was quoted as saying United "must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending".

Pochettino is unlikely to admit it publicly, but behind closed doors must have similarly widespread concerns even at this early stage. United have not found themselves in the bottom two after 11 games in 40 years.

Sir Alex Ferguson was brought in as their eventual saviour that winter, but turning the tide on this United side is a significantly bigger ask.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Are there personnel at his disposal who could improve matters? Potentially. Neville did pinpoint a back four of Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Diego Dalot who could at least get United out of their defensive slump.

"It's a poor back four, but it's their best back four. It could compete," he added. "But the one that started today and finished against Villa a few weeks ago, that'll get you relegated."

There is good news and bad news. Neville's quartet are unbeaten in every game they have started together since the start of 2023/24 - and can boast a 70-per-cent win ratio. Unfortunately for Pochettino, that only amounts to 10 games across more than three seasons, owing largely to availability.

But that still does not solve the problem of their limp attack. Of the 22 players to have attempted a shot for the club this season, 19 have under-performed their xG, and the three who have not, Benjamin Sesko, Joshua Zirkzee and Youri Tielemans, have scored only a solitary goal apiece.

There remain huge question marks over the Man Utd dressing room, its commitment and a lack of leadership which permeated into the public sphere in the final weeks of Michael Carrick's reign. Though Pochettino's players have shown they can perform when they want to. Carrick himself knows that better than anyone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

But his successor barely has time to address it over the next few weeks, with only one free midweek between now and the end of 2026 - and even then he has a trip to the Emirates, live on Sky Sports on December 20, to face at the end of his first uninterrupted week on the training pitch.

By that point United will be almost half-way through the Premier League season - and alarm bells will be ringing even louder if they still find themselves in the quagmire, especially with rock bottom Crystal Palace and promoted Coventry to come before then.

But might even that prove problematic for Pochettino?

"If you look at the strength of the Premier League this season, in terms of what we would call the teams you'd expect to be mid-table or near the bottom - it's probably as strong as it's ever been," said Carragher.

"There's no poor teams. There's not many great teams, but there's no poor teams.

#745. Aspyn Ovard Details Decision to Have Baby No. 3 Amid Daughter's Cancer

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star Aspyn Ovard shared why she decided to have a third baby after her daughter Cove, 7, was diagnosed with cancer: "Being pregnant saved my life."

Aspyn Ovard is shedding light on her motherhood journey.

Over a week after the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star shared her daughter Cove’s terminal cancer diagnosis on the Hulu series premiere, she explained why she decided to grow her family and have a third baby with then-husband Parker Ferris amid their eldest daughter’s health battle.

“I didn’t want my other child to grow up alone,” Ovard—mom to daughters Lola, 5, and Elle, 2, with Ferris—shared in a Nov. 21 YouTube vlog, answering a fan’s question about her decision to have more kids. “I did decide to have another baby. I did do it on kind of a crazy timeline.”

“It was a lot to be doing all of that with everything we were going through, but I just knew that that was what was right for our family,” she continued. “I didn’t want a really big age gap, so that was something that I put myself through and did for my family and for my daughters.”

And although it was difficult, the YouTuber emphasized that she doesn’t regret her choice.

“I have never felt like I shouldn’t have done it on that timeline,” she stressed. “I’m very glad that I did.”

And while the 30-year-old and Ferris were in the midst of navigating Cove’s diagnosis at the time, Ovard noted that being pregnant ultimately made her stronger.

“That was the one thing I could focus on,” she recalled, “and the one thing that was in my control.”

Though the reality star admitted that it’s difficult to discuss that time, she shared that pregnancy “kept me going.”

“My marriage was nowhere near in a place to be able to make it through something like this,” she said during an emotional confessional. “We weren't even going to make it through before this happened.”

#744. IFA 'positive' over upgrades needed for World Cup

Windsor Park would require 5,000 additional seats to host games at the 2035 World Cup

The Irish Football Association's director of women's football Angela Platt said the organisation is "still working through" plans with the Northern Ireland government to ensure there is funding available to make the necessary upgrades to Windsor Park in time for the 2035 World Cup.

It was confirmed on Monday that Northern Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales, the only bidders for the tournament in nine years' time, had been ratified as co-hosts.

Of the 19 venues proposed by the 'All Together' bid, Belfast's Windsor Park is the sole stadium in Northern Ireland, but would require an additional 5,000 seats to its current capacity of 18,500 as well as changes to the pitch and floodlights.

"We're obviously working with our government partners who've committed their support to help us do that, and we'll continue our endeavours to make sure that we work towards that," Platt told BBC NI's Stephen Watson.

"We know that the Northern Ireland Executive has given a commitment to back us and do whatever they can to support us in our endeavours to make sure we're ready for that hosting of the Women's World Cup in 2035.

"We have a few years to make sure we work through that."

Northern Ireland was involved in a similar bid to host games at Euro 2028, but plans for fixtures in Belfast at that tournament fell through when the government said it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in the required timescale.

Platt said that "was in the past" and that the organisation were focused on the work required to avoid any repeat.

"We're still working towards making sure that it does happen and we're positive. We know that the work is there to make sure that it happens," she added.

"It's obviously disappointing when something that people work so hard to put together doesn't come to fruition, but certainly that's in the past for us.

"From our perspective, working for women's football, this is a great opportunity for Northern Ireland to get behind this and actually make sure that we do everything we can to host our Women's World Cup games here."

UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa confirms

Plans to increase Windsor Park capacity to 23,750

There is no guarantee that, even as co-hosts, there would an automatic qualification spot for Northern Ireland.

The side last qualified for a major tournament at Euro 2022 and Platt believes bringing the World Cup to the country has the potential to "inspire a new generation".

"I think it can have a huge impact. We've always been blessed that we have had our women's team involved in the Women's Euros in 2022, and through my role, I get to visit other nations hosting tournaments such as this," she said.

"I was in Sydney for the Women's World Cup (2023) and obviously saw the impact hosting a tournament like that had in New Zealand and Australia, and likewise for the Euros in England and Switzerland recently.

"That impact is significant. It's the growth of the game, it's the engagement, it's the legacy. So much positivity can come out of hosting major tournaments and we're excited to play our part in this and it can only have benefits for Northern Ireland in general."

#740. From conceding seven to Hull heroics - how Tzolakis recovered to defy Brighton

McBurnie stoppage-time double earns Hull win over 10-man Brighton

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic used one word to describe the performance of his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis in Sunday's 2-0 Premier League win against Brighton.

"Unbelievable," he told Match of the Day.

"Especially after the international break, which was very difficult for him."

Tzolakis' previous outing had been for Greece against the Netherlands in the Uefa Nations League, where he and his side were humbled 7-0 by the hosts in Amsterdam.

Nine days later, his contribution to the Tigers' first league victory since 29 August was every bit as important as that of striker Oli McBurnie, who netted both goals in second-half stoppage time against the second-placed Seagulls.

Tzolakis made a series of top saves to keep the highest scorers in the top flight at bay and, when Brighton full-back Costinha was sent off in the 89th minute for a second bookable offence, the hosts seized their opportunity to clinch only their third win following their Premier League return.

McBurnie said the 24-year-old stopper had "kept Hull in a few games" this season and the club were "lucky to have him", while Tzolakis told Sky Sports: "We are a unit and a team.

"We play for each other. We showed a good team effort and we deserved the three points."

McBurnie scores stoppage-time double as Hull stun Brighton

How 'outstanding' Tzolakis kept Brighton at bay

With the opportunity to move three points behind leaders Arsenal, Brighton looked most likely to score for long spells of Sunday's game, but just could not find a way past former Olympiacos goalkeeper Tzolakis, who joined Hull in August for a reported Â£20m fee.

He got down to make a vital block early on to deny Diego Gomez, who had slid in to meet a low cross from the left wing. It was the first of several occasions the Paraguay international would be frustrated in front of goal.

Tzolakis then raced out spreadeagled to foil Georginio Rutter with an outstretched left hand - a stop that BBC Radio 5 Live pundit and former striker Clinton Morrison described as "Peter Schmeichel-esque", referring to the legendary Denmark keeper.

Second-half efforts from distance by Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk were dealt with, too.

Yasin Ayari went close with a thumping strike against the bar and when Brighton substitute Charalampos Kostoulas pounced on a short backpass to go through one-on-one, Tzolakis got a hand on his Greece team-mate's shot and Regan Slater was back on the goalline to head the ball to safety.

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy, a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said: "We saw again how important Tzolakis is for Hull. He had one of those days where he was always in the right place at the right time.

"When you are a Hull player and you see the kind of saves Tzolakis made when he spread himself and kept it out with his foot, you start thinking that it could be your day.

"It happens a lot in football and, on the flip side, Brighton will have been thinking, 'are we ever going to score here?'."

Hull made a superb start to the campaign after being promoted via the Championship play-offs in May.

They followed victories against Manchester United and Coventry with a draw against Aston Villa - all without conceding a goal.

The Tigers had not won since that 1-0 success at Coventry until beating Brighton - but they are one of four top-flight sides still unbeaten at home and have not lost any fixture by more than a one-goal margin.

They lost 1-0 to champions Arsenal before the international break and Scotland forward McBurnie told Match of the Day: "We know we can make it difficult for the top teams in the league and we've proved that in the past two games.

"We want to make it as difficult as we can for teams to come here and make the MKM Stadium a tough place to come. It's proving that way so far, so long may it continue."

#739. Three years on NI Women finally have friendlies again

Northern Ireland's friendly double-header against Greece will be live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website

Tuesday, 18 July 2023 was the last time Northern Ireland Women played a friendly.

Under interim manager Gail Redmond, NI produced a fine display to beat Czech Republic 2-0 in Opava.

Just over three and a half years later, Northern Ireland will have not one but two friendly fixtures, with Michael McArdle's side taking on Greece in an Inver Park double-header on 27 November and 1 December.

A lot has changed for NI since that last friendly, but, having two pressure-free games finally offers McArdle an opportunity to experiment with tactics and personnel as they take the first step towards building for Euro 2029 qualifying.

Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies

Greece were beaten by England in the first round of the World Cup play-offs

Only eight players who were in the squad for that friendly win are in the current crop over three years on.

Rebecca McKenna, Rebecca Holloway and Simone Magill started while Lauren Wade, Kerry Beattie and Joely Andrews came off the bench.

Fi Morgan and Chloe McCarron were unused substitutes.

Goalkeeper Lilie Woods made her debut, Marissa Callaghan captained the side and Sarah McFadden and Beattie scored the goals in a rare away win.

A month after that friendly victory, Tanya Oxtoby arrived to take over as Kenny Shiels' permanent successor.

She eventually left to take over at Newcastle United in November 2025 and all 26 of her games as NI manager were competitive fixtures.

The introduction of the Nations League and its close ties to Euro and World Cup qualification admittedly left little room in what is now a stacked international women's calendar for friendly games.

During Oxtoby's tenure, NI had two Nations League campaigns sandwiched between Euro 2025 qualifiers.

After falling to Iceland in their Nations League promotion/relegation play off last October, they opted against seeking any friendlies at the end of November as they looked for a successor to Oxtoby.

The competitive games kept coming and Kris Lindsay was then in interim charge of NI's first two 2027 World Cup qualifiers before McArdle took over in April for the four remaining group games and the subsequent first-round play-off defeat against Portugal.

With NI not involved in the second round of the World Cup play-offs while many others are in the upcoming window, McArdle has decided to get the squad together for two friendlies.

With such a young squad at his disposal and with McArdle still relatively new to the job, he is relishing the chance to have the players in camp for an extended period and for NI to test themselves against decent opposition.

"We don't want friendly games in this window, we want to be in the play-offs but we had planned for both [scenarios], this has been a long-term plan," he said.

"Greece I specifically selected because I knew we couldn't draw them in the Nations League as we're in the same pot, but also they're a strong nation who are progressing well and are close to ourselves in the rankings.

"They'll be a real test for us. It was very deliberate selection."

Northern Ireland suffered a 7-1 aggregate defeat in the first round World Cup play-off against Portugal

McArdle wants NI to be "more horrible to play against" and feels they will work on that in this camp as well as what they do when in possession to trouble opponents.

Greece, like Northern Ireland, exited the World Cup play-offs at the first round after an aggregate 8-1 defeat to England.

They had been in good form before back-to-back defeats by the Lionesses, winning five games this year as they topped Group C4 to seal promotion to League B.

"It gives us two games to try and win first and foremost because we need to develop the winning mentality, but also to test some things because a lot of the identity and how we play, after six competitive games, there is still work to do particularly in possession, we've not quite done that yet," McArdle continued.

"That identity that we never give up and are constantly going, that is the case for the group, but we have to improve the athleticism and the duels to bridge the gap to qualification to tournaments."

Qualifying for the 2029 Euros in Germany does not begin until 2028, but McArdle's side have a testing Nations League campaign to prepare for next year.

They have been drawn against Poland, Finland and Belarus and the Scot revealed that he is already planning ahead for potential friendly opponents for next year's November/December international window to maximise time spent with his squad if they are not in the Nations League play-offs.

"There's also the importance of taking all the activity available to us and that's crucial for us growing and moving forward.

"We're already planning for next November/December window and selecting opponents because there is a deliberate strategy how we evolve the group.

"Part of that is strategically picking opponents which will help us grow. The friendlies, in a sense it's not competitive games, but we'll approach them in the same way."
