#702. One of football's most-hyped 16-year-olds - what next for JJ Gabriel?

JJ Gabriel featured for Manchester United's senior team in pre-season

It has been one of the biggest transfer sagas of the year - around a player who has never played competitive football.

Forward JJ Gabriel, who has recently turned 16, walked out on Manchester United in September and now has a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

Before even playing a senior game - barring friendlies - he has told Spanish newspaper Marca his "dream is to win the Ballon d'Or".

Gabriel's real name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill - with Cypriot and Irish lineage - but he changed his name, reportedly for commercial purposes.

His father, London-born Joe O'Cearuill, played twice for the Republic of Ireland - but the highest level he played at club level was a loan spell with Brighton in League One and one minute in the Uefa Cup with St Patrick's Athletic. He has been actively involved in his son's career.

Gabriel was scheduled to become Manchester United's youngest ever player in the Carabao Cup against Brighton on 16 September, but had told the club he planned to leave by then.

How long will Gabriel have to wait for a first-team debut now? In the past 10 years Real have only handed two debuts to 17-year-olds and none to a 16-year-old.

When Real boss Jose Mourinho was asked about Gabriel on Friday, he said: "I don't have a feeling [about Gabriel]. I don't have a feeling with players who don't work with me."

In fact, Real have not even announced anything yet - despite Gabriel posting a 50-second video montage on social media saying goodbye to United this week.

Madrid-bound Gabriel posts farewell Man Utd message

Why schoolboys have become a huge part of football's transfer market

For a while now Madrid have been getting the best young talents early and turning them into Galacticos before they cost in excess of 100m euros.

Vinicius Junior and Rodrygo came that way, then Endrick - and Gabriel is seen as the next.

It fits the policy run by Jose Angel Sanchez, the director general, and Juni Calafat, head of scouting. It is a long-term bet on one of the most promising young players in the international game.

Barcelona looked at him too, and backed away because the commissions were too high. Madrid believe in the player so much that they were willing to pay whatever it took to get the deal done.

The expectations are very high and the aim is for him to reach the first team. They want him at Castilla - Real's reserve team - but the situation right now does not allow it.

Castilla and Real Madrid C cannot sign players until January, so for the time being he is expected to play for the Juvenil - the under-18s.

Madrid also learned from the Martin Odegaard period that training with the first team while playing for the B side is a bad idea. So the plan is a spell in the B side, and when he is ready, Gabriel jumps straight into the first team.

Where Madrid are less happy is with how things have unfolded. Madrid wanted to set the timing themselves and be discreet, because they do not want problems with Manchester United and do not want to upset anyone. At Real Madrid, nobody is bigger than the club.

The idea was to keep everything quiet until January and announce it then. But with Gabriel already training in Madrid, the secret was never going to last.

"Players are moving to him because his reputation is that he'll get you a move to a bigger club," one Premier League club source told BBC Sport.

Dubai-based Barat does not just consider himself a super-agent, but a "boutique" super-agent.

Born in Iran and raised in London, Barat says he fell into football almost by accident after many years in international business.

After initially working as an intermediary at low-level clubs, he founded Epic Sports in January 2020.

His major football experience before that? The football game Championship Manager.

"I was always trading players," he told ESPN this year. "I was obsessed with every single player around the world."

This was not just about living out a fantasy in the real world. Barat was drawn into the profession because of the vast sums agents can earn in commission.

What makes his agency "boutique"? Unlike the top operations which have a huge number of players on their books, Epic Sports aims to have just 22 - two for each position.

This, Barat argues, ensures there is never any conflict of interest in how he represents his players.

Barat offers bespoke management of a player's career and came to prominence in the summer of 2025 when 15 of his players moved on.

This included Dean Huijsen joining Real Madrid, Nicolas Jackson moving to Bayern Munich and Xavi Simons signing for Tottenham Hotspur. Noni Madueke left Chelsea for Arsenal, and the Gunners signed Piero Hincapie.

This led to Barat being named Golden Boy Best Agent for the second time in three years.

Yet he is largely the figurehead, with agents working on his behalf around Europe. For instance, Epic has three other agents registered with the English Football Association (FA).

Barat, who also brokered Moises Caicedo's move to Chelsea, says he uses social media, and in particular influencer Fabrizio Romano, to amplify stories and agree transfers on his terms.

"Ali Barat redefines the game again," read an Epic Sports press release to announce Jackson's loan move to Bayern. No other agency seems to promote itself in this way.

The largely AI-generated video which announced Gabriel had joined Epic Sports was right on brand.

Gabriel's deal is part of a new venture: Epic Future - and this presents an ethical problem.

"It is about targeting the biggest young players, especially where they're not necessarily on the longest contracts," a Premier League source said. "And move them overseas for cheap fees.

"The original club will get a few 100,000 euros if that, and everyone else will hoover up millions and millions and millions - including his family."

Transferring a player to Europe also opens the door to future sell-on fees for an agent, which is against FA regulations.

It is this new focus on younger players which has started to cause friction at some top clubs.

No club wants to lose players they have spent years developing for nothing, only for an agent to reap the rewards.

Manchester United had to work hard 18 months ago to convince JJ Gabriel and his family that Old Trafford was the right place to further his football education.

The big question is, did they overpromise in doing so?

Sources close to the player eventually felt they were let down and United did not deliver on what was expected.

Certainly around Gabriel's pre-season minutes and presence in the squad for the Champions League opener against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK, which it was felt would be a perfect opportunity for the youngster to make his debut.

By the time the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton came round, there was no faith Gabriel would be brought on. Given United lost 3-2, there is merit in that stance.

The secondary elements are where will Gabriel develop the most?

United's academy is one of the best in England at producing young players, but given his size, will the forward benefit more from being in a less physical environment?

There has been a lot of sniping around his decision to leave United, but his stats are impressive and he is clearly a player of huge potential. United would certainly have wished the situation had not unfolded the way it has.

#700. Reese's Heir Brad Reese Reveals Dad's Eerie Deathbed Confession

Reese's heir Brad Reese shared that his dad Dick Reese's 2025 deathbed confession is the reason he's publicly called out  Hershey for allegedly replacing the candy's ingredients.

Brad Reese isn't sugarcoating a recent family revelation.

Nine months after the grandson of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups inventor H.B. Reese accused The Hershey Company of "quietly replacing" the candy's signature chocolate and peanut with different ingredients, he revealed how dad Charles Richard "Dick" Reese's biggest regret led to his new mission.

"'I don't wanna die because I don't wanna go to heaven,'" Brad revealed Dick told him before his 2005 death in an interview with The Daily Mail published Nov. 22. His dad added that he was afraid to reunite with H.B. because he "double-crossed him" by selling the company outside the family.

Though Brad—who noted that he still holds shares in Hershey—has no formal role in, or ownership of, Reese's since his dad and five uncles sold the rights to produce the candy to the company in 1963, no amount of sweet-talking would keep him from advocating for the peanut butter cups' legacy.

"He made me promise if he gave me my shares I would never sell them," he said of their conversation. "There's no amount of money that would send me packing. I'm not doing this for money, and I'm not doing this for a position on the board."

Brad's decision to unwrap his feud with Hershey—which went on to introduce other products like Reese's Pieces in 1978 and Reese's Puffs in 1994—turned a deeply personal situation public when he criticized the company online earlier this year.

"I'm doing it because I believe in it, that's the most important thing," he clarified. "There's nothing that the Hershey company can do to financially hurt me."

The U.S. Army veteran couldn't resist publicly criticizing the major chocolate manufacturer, alleging in a February LinkedIn post that Hershey replaced "milk chocolate with compound coatings and peanut butter with peanut-butter-style crèmes across multiple Reese's products" in recent years.

"Right now, the Reese's story is diverging from what's inside Reese's products," he continued. "I'm not asking for nostalgia. I'm asking for alignment. For truth in Reese's brand stewardship. For a corporate narrative from The Hershey Company that reflects the Reese's product consumers are actually receiving."

Hershey disputed Brad's claims, telling E! News in a statement at the time that the peanut butter cups are still "made the same way they always have been, starting with roasting fresh peanuts to make our unique, one-of-a-kind peanut butter that is then combined with milk chocolate."

However, the company noted that other Reese's products may have different ingredients.

"As we've grown and expanded the Reese's product line, we make product recipe adjustments that allow us to make new shapes, sizes and innovations that Reese's fans have come to love and ask for," Hershey continued, "while always protecting the essence of what makes Reese's unique and special: the perfect combination of chocolate and peanut butter."

As Brad continues to speak out about Reese's peanut butter-chocolate flavor, keep reading for more major nutty feuds.

The Sex and the City costars had dodged feud rumors for years, but they were reignited after Cattrall decided not to return for a third movie and made comments about her SLP that raised eyebrows.

"What was your reaction to Kim Cattrall telling Piers Morgan that you were never friends just colleagues?" Andy Cohen asked Parker on a September 2017 episode of Watch What Happens Live.

As she explained, "Just...heartbroken. I mean that whole week, you and I spoke about it because I was just...I don't know I found it really upsetting because that's, you know, that's not the way I recall our experience."

"So...it's sad but I'm kind of...I don't know, I always think that what ties us together is this singular experience is the thing," she continued. "It was a professional experience but it became personal because it was years and years of our lives. So I'm hoping that that sort of eclipses anything that's been recently spoken. That many years spent doing something so special that people had a connection with is such a privileged."

And though they didn't film scenes together, Cattrall did make a small appearance on And Just Like That.

During a 2022 TikTok challenge, JoJo Siwa described Candace Cameron Bure as the "rudest" celebrity, later explaining that she felt snubbed when Bure once refused to take a picture with her on a red carpet. Shortly after the dig, however, the Full House alum apologized: "I kind of broke your 11-year-old heart. I didn't take a picture with you. Ugh! I feel crummy, I feel—JoJo, I'm so sorry."

The two made amends. But months later, Cameron Bure was asked if she expects the Great American Family network, of which she serves as chief creative officer, to feature same-sex couples as leads in holiday movies. She said no, adding, "I think that Great American Family will keep traditional marriage at the core."

Siwa, who came out as a member of the LGBTQ+ community in 2021, wrote on Instagram that the actress' comment is "rude and hurtful to a whole community of people."

In August 2022, Morris and Pope traded harsh words with Aldean, wife of fellow country star Jason Aldean, after she shared an Instagram Reel of herself applying makeup, writing, "I'd really like to thank my parents for not changing my gender when I went through my tomboy phase. I love this girly life."

Berk (pictured second from left) addressed rumors of a falling out with France (middle) in January 2024, two months after he announced his exit from Queer Eye after eight seasons.

"I want people to know that Tan and I—we will be fine," he told Vanity Fair. "There was a situation, and that's between Tan and I, and it has nothing to do with the show. It was something personal that had been brewing—and nothing romantic, just to clarify that."

In March 2024, France responded to allegations that he had campaigned to replace Berk on Queer Eye with his friend Jeremiah Brent.

"Netflix and the production companies did a full-on casting. I didn't put my friend up for the job. They ended up getting it because they were the best person for the job," he said on Instagram. "But I didn't get them hired by getting rid of somebody else."

In September 2023, while playing a game called Stir the Pot with her daughter Kelly Osbourne on E! News, Sharon said the That '70s Show alum was the rudest celebrity she had ever met, branding him, a "rude, rude, rude, rude little boy" and a "dastardly little thing."

Back in June 2021, the Hole frontwoman accused Rodrigo of copying her band's album cover for a promotional photo without giving credit, prompting the Disney alum to respond, "Love u and live through this sooooo much."

however, it seemed their hatchet was buried when Love replied, "Olivia - you're welcome. My favorite florist is in Notting Hill, London! Dm me for deets! I look forward to reading your note [winking face emoji]."

Fans of The Hills will remember that iconic line, delivered by Conrad on the season three premiere. Their feud began when Montag started dating her now-husband Spencer Pratt, and hit its peak when Conrad accused her and Pratt of starting a rumor that she had made a sex tape with then-boyfriend Jason Wahler.

The costars reignited their ongoing feud in 2017 when Gibson publicly called out Johnson on Instagram after the Fast and Furious 9 release date was pushed back to April 2020. That same day, it was announced that a Fast and Furious spinoff starring Johnson and Jason Statham would hit theaters in 2019. The following month, Gibson threatened to quit Fast 9 if Johnson was in the movie.

Gibson then opened up about the feud, telling Van Lathan on The Red Pill podcast, "I have yet to talk to The Rock to this day, and we will have a conversation." He shared that he did have a chat with the former wrestler's producing partner, but not the actor himself.

"I found myself being the messenger on behalf of various people associated to the franchise, but stupid me was the only one who went public about those feelings, which is my own fault," gibson said. "It's not professional, it's not cool."

Swift and Perry had been in a feud for years, with their rift even allegedly inspiring the former's song "Bad Blood." The drama, which reportedly started over a backup dancer and competing tours, came to an end after Perry sent Swift a literal olive branch before her Reputation Tour kickoff in 2018.

"So I just got to my dressing room and found this actual olive branch," Swift said in an Instagram video. "This mean so much."

She captioned the video, "Thank you Katy."

Since when has lip-syncing been live? Sorry about that, but I think everyone who lip-syncs in public on stage, when you pay like 75 quid to see them, should be shot."

The former Grey's Anatomy star sparked a feud with the series creator in 2008 when she removed her name from the Emmy Awards consideration. Heigl stated that her reason for the move was because she wasn't "given the material to warrant a nomination."

Rhimes later opened up about Heigl's decision during an interview with Oprah Winfrey on Oprah's Next Chapter in 2012. "On some level it stung and on some level I was not surprised," she said. "When people show you who they are, believe them. I carry that [mantra] with me a lot. It has served me well."

It was the New York Fashion Week fight heard 'round the world when Nicki and Cardi got into a heated altercation at the Harper's Bazaar Icon party. The following month, Cardi opened up about the catalyst for the fight with Nicki.

"For a while now she's been taking a lot of shots at me," Cardi said in W magazine's Art Issue. "I spoke to her twice before, and we came to an understanding. But she kept it going."

The real spark of the fight came when Cardi saw that Nicki had allegedly liked and then unliked a tweet about Cardi's parenting skills, which Nicki has denied.

"I was going to make millions off my Bruno Mars tour, and I sacrificed that to stay with my daughter," Cardi continued. "I love my daughter. I'm a good-ass f--king mom. So for somebody that don't have a child to like that comment? So many people want to say that party wasn't the time or the place, but I'm not going to catch another artist in the grocery store or down the block."

Tension between Kanye and Taylor first started in 2009, when the "Stronger" rapper took the stage during her acceptance speech at the MTV Video Music Awards. Years later, the two would make up and even become friends, but that came to an end in 2016 after the release of his song "Famous," in which he name-checks the "End Game" singer.

In February 2025, one day before the Grammys, Kanye updated his Instagram to follow only Taylor. He added no further comment, and his fellow musician did not respond publicly to the move.

Carey and J.Lo's supposed feud started when the Queen of Christmas was asked to give her opinion on several singers during a 2003 German TV interview. When asked her opinion on Lopez, she replied, "I don't know her."

#699. Holloway sacked by Swindon after two seasons

Ian Holloway surpassed 1,000 games managing in English football during his time at Swindon

Manager Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon Town after just over two years in charge.

The Robins' 2-0 loss at Newport County on Saturday left them 17th in League Two and was their fourth successive defeat in all competitions - conceding 10 goals in the process.

They have won only two of their past 15 matches, and Holloway last month described himself as a "dead man walking" if Swindon's form did not turn around.

"Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season," read a Swindon statement.

Swindon's Holloway labels himself dead man walking

Lewis double fires County to victory against Swindon

"However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

"This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart."

Coaches Gavin Gunning and Steve Mildenhall will take charge of the first team on an interim basis, with David Carney assisting them.

Holloway was appointed in October 2024 until the end of that season, with Swindon one place above the relegation zone.

He surpassed 1,000 games managing in English football two months later and signed a two-year contract in March 2025, having steered Swindon into play-off contention.

Promotion was the aim last season, with Holloway issuing a rallying call at the start of the campaign for Swindon to be the "team I believe we can" be.

They were in the automatic promotion spots in February, but only three wins in their last 13 games, including a 2-1 defeat by Chesterfield in a must-win final match, meant they missed out on the play-offs.

Although Swindon won three of their first five league games this season, they are without a win in their past five and have scored one goal in that time.

Ian Holloway was ushered away by stewards after approaching Swindon's fans after Saturday's loss at Newport County

Andrew Hawes, BBC Radio Wiltshire Swindon Town commentator

This season has largely consisted of feeling Swindon are two games away from a crisis and Australia-based chairman Clem Morfuni's arrival in the country to see deserved defeats by Newport and Grimsby finally made it one.

The team have consistently struggled to create goals and chances despite having League Two's player of the year Aaron Drinan, a rare exception to a chronic injury list.

The fans' energy for Holloway had grown thin, and sometimes vice versa.

Being ushered away by a steward at Rodney Parade as his last act may be a summary of how both felt about each other.

But there is a clear feel of stagnation at Swindon - and that means putting another manager on the chopping block is no guarantee of improvement.

Megha Ganne won the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage as 27 tour cards were claimed for the 2027 season, with five-time USA Solheim Cup team member Megan Khang among those successful.

Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is returning to the LPGA Tour, on which she's made 259 starts since 2016, winning the 2023 CPKC Women's Open.

The top-25 finishers and ties at the conclusion of the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying were awarded LPGA Tour status for next year.

American Ganne won the final stage outright on 23 under, one shot clear of Shannon Tan and Julia Gregg in a tie for second. Min Sun7 Kim was fourth on 21 under and Xiaowen Yin one further back in fifth.

Ganne, the 2025 US Amateur champion, had actually already secured her 2027 LPGA Tour status by entering the week by finishing 11-15 on the Epson Tour.

Gregg, who finished in a share of second, has never previously had a start on the LPGA Tour.

"It feels unreal," the 25-year-old American said after clinching her place. "It's been my dream since I was four years old to play on the LPGA and now that I finally did it."

The WTGL season continues on Wednesday when Lottie Woad's Boston Common chase their first win of the campaign against Charley Hull's Atlanta Drive GC. Live coverage begins on Wednesday from 1am on Sky Sports Golf.

#697. Watford set to appoint former Romania boss Iordanescu

Edward Iordanescu's most recent job was with Legia Warsaw, who he left in October 2025

Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager.

BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge.

The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT).

Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16.

Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025.

It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland.

Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

#696. Build for the future climate — or waste trillions of dollars

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Saroj Kanta Mishra is a professor and leads the Department of Science and Technology Centre of Excellence for Climate Information at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, Delhi, India.

Reservoirs need to be constructed in ways that help to avoid water shortages as heatwaves increase. Credit: Ander Gillenea/AFP via Getty

“Prepare for El Niño”, the World Meteorological Organization warned earlier this year. Governments are responding by adjusting agricultural practices and securing water supplies. But climate measures should not begin when a hazardous event approaches, they should be part of a wider strategy of planning for a warmer future.

Repeated disasters cause immense disruption to people’s lives and livelihoods, and the economic loss and damage can add up to trillions of dollars. Climate warnings and actions taken in anticipation of disasters can help to reduce the impact on people and economies. But their effectiveness is constrained by existing limitations, such as a community’s access to resources and infrastructure.

Such vulnerabilities must be addressed at their source, when decisions about development and infrastructure are being made, so that climate risks are reduced through better planning rather than through reactive responses to individual events. Decisions about the location and capacity of reservoirs, agricultural drainage systems and the design of cities and transport infrastructure, for instance, cannot be changed easily once they have been made.

Much of what is being built now will shape societies for decades. To meet global climate and development objectives by 2030, nearly US$7 trillion of infrastructure investment is needed annually1. Global annual infrastructure spending is projected to increase from $4.4 trillion in 2024 to $6.9 trillion by 20502. But it will be wasted if projects are designed inadequately for the climate conditions that people will face.

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too

The super El Niño is more than a climate shock — it’s a health one, too

Decisions for development projects are being hampered because climate projections are often not integrated into planning processes. Another challenge is the limited availability of reliable, decision-relevant climate information for the 5–30-year period — an intermediate timescale between seasonal forecasts and long-term climate projections that is particularly relevant for planning major infrastructure such as roads and reservoirs3.

Climate services can provide this information. Scientists can improve climate projections. Development planners can assess projects. But unless these functions are connected within the development process, the system as a whole remains reactive.

A common operating system would change that. Government ministries that oversee development would determine which planning decisions need to consider climate information. Planning institutions would ensure that climate assessments are undertaken and considered as part of investment approval for climate-sensitive projects. Climate agencies would provide the scientific information, which would improve both planning and science. Here, I outline how such a system would work.

A central government planning institution should establish a small climate-planning unit within it, not separately. Corresponding units could be set up in state or subnational planning institutions when appropriate. In countries without central planning institutions, the same functions could be assigned to existing government institutions.

The central unit would set common standards, consolidate information needs across sectors and jurisdictions, coordinate with national climate agencies and ensure that climate considerations are incorporated into the planning and appraisal of projects of national significance. Subnational units would apply the framework to local projects and feed emerging requirements back to the central unit.

Responsibilities should be made explicit. Ministries should identify the climate information needed to support various sectors. Planning institutions would coordinate those needs and ensure that such climate information informs investment decisions. Climate agencies would produce the underlying scientific information and ensure its technical accuracy and quality.

This division matters. The proposal is not to make development planners become climate scientists, nor to make climate agencies become development authorities. It is to give them a permanent institutional connection.

The rules governing public investment in development should be changed to follow this principle: funding for a major climate-sensitive project should not be approved without a demonstration that it has been designed for the climate it is expected to face.

Governments should request climate assessments for large, long-lived and climate-sensitive projects before approving funds. Assessments should be provided early enough in the process to influence the location, technology, scale and design of a project. For a new reservoir, for example, the relevant planning unit would identify the climate conditions that the reservoir is likely to face during its operational lifetime, with implications for where and how it is built.

A climate-planning unit would not decide whether the project should proceed; it would certify that the relevant climate risks have been assessed and that reasonable alternatives have been considered. Its assessment would be considered as part of an investment appraisal alongside economic, technical, social and environmental factors.

To be effective, the system must connect three functions: development demand, climate analysis and investment approval.

Ministries should periodically identify the climate information needed for their forthcoming development decisions. The central planning unit should consolidate these requests and work with climate agencies to determine what information can be provided, what projects require fresh analysis and when investment for climate observations, modelling or scientific capacity is needed.

Kenya’s government is implementing measures to reduce flooding from rivers.Credit: James Wakibia/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty

This comprehensive approach would provide climate scientists with clear directives from the development system. It would encourage them to improve climate projections for specific regions, over a 5–30-year typical planning horizon, and for distinct sectors. It would also reduce the need for individual development projects to commission their own climate analyses, which can be patchy and inconsistent.

An analysis of six generations of assessment reports from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change found, for instance, that inconsistent climate projections across many low- and middle-income countries were complicating adaptation and long-term planning efforts4. For example, in some regions, precipitation was projected by one assessment to increase, and by the next to decrease, with successive views bouncing back and forth.

Such disagreements undermine a region’s ability to make long-term investments. They increase the likelihood of costly misallocation of funds, maladaptation to climate risks and infrastructure being developed that is ill-suited to future climate conditions. Dams, cities and transport corridors cannot be easily redesigned or rebuilt once constructed.

This challenge is compounded by the fact that climate models perform poorly across many climate-vulnerable regions. In South Asia, for example, simulations of temperature and precipitation can differ from observed values by as much as 25% and 100%, respectively5. Such biases limit the reliability of model-based climate information for guiding long-term development decisions.

That’s why the proposed climate-informed planning units would ensure that climate agencies’ work is guided by clearly articulated development needs and that the information they provide is reliable and fit for development planning. Importantly, they would not be a replacement for other climate services, which can remain focused on providing accurate information for a wide range of sectors6,7. The aim is to bridge a specific gap between climate information and development.

A climate assessment for a development project should not become obsolete as soon as the work is approved. Both central and subnational planning units should regularly monitor whether new climate observations or scientific assessments change the climate risks identified. If they do, an updated assessment should be returned to the planning authority.

Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming

Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming

The units should evaluate whether the climate information generated by the system is useful. Regular technical reviews would compare climate projections with observations and assess whether the information remains fit for planning purposes. Institutional reviews conducted by climate-planning units could also examine whether big projects have incorporated climate foresight and whether it influenced their designs.

These reviews would create a feedback loop. Development decisions would determine what information is needed, which could be satisfied by climate-science and investment-appraisal processes. Data from implemented projects would then be fed back into the system to update climate information and plans going forwards.

#695. The Altruists: Where Sam Bankman-Fried & Caroline Ellison Are Today

Years after disgraced crypto couple Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison reported to prison, their lives became subject of the Netflix series The Altruists, starring Anthony Doyle and Julia Garner.

You don’t need a seed phrase to relive the rise and fall of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison.

All it takes, these days, is a Netflix login, as the former couple’s journey becoming major players in the cryptocurrency world until the collapse of the bitcoin FTX led to an investigation and their respective legal battles takes center stage in the new Netflix series The Altruists. But it also begs the question: what are Bankman-Fried and Ellison up—played by Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner in the limited series—to now?

For Bankman-Fried, his whereabouts will remain in the public record for the foreseeable future—his release date is currently December 15, 2043—as he serves 25-year prison sentence after being convicted on seven federal charges of fraud, conspiracy and money laundering in November 2023. The 34-year-old, who had pleaded not guilty, was also ordered to pay $11 billion in forfeiture.

He and Ellison were accused—along with other FTX execs—of using billions of dollars in stolen money from customer accounts to make risky investments and using company funds to buy real estate and make political donations.

The co-founder of Bahamas-based cryptocurrency exchange FTX—once valued at $30 billion before the company filed for bankruptcy in Nov. 2022—is currently serving out his sentence at the low-security FCI Lompoc I prison in Lompoc, Calif., per the Federal Bureau of Prisons.

Bankman-Friend also remained active since reporting to prison in TK, detailing his time in the same cell block as Sean “Diddy” Combs while they were being held in the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, New York, expressing to Tucker Carlson in March 2025 that they were "two of the most famous prisoners in the world."

He also didn’t shy away from Boyle, with the House of Guinness actor detailing their email correspondences.

"I was really bowled over by his intelligence,” Boyle said on the Today show Nov. 20. "Even through emails I was like, ‘This guy is a savant.’ He’s so, so clever. Really, really interesting guy."

For her part, Ellison has kept a lower profile. The one-time Alameda Research co-CEO was sentenced to two years in prison in Sept. 2024 for financial fraud and conspiracy after accepting a plea deal two years prior in order to cooperate with federal investigators, per Today, citing court records.

The 32-year-old ended up testifying against Bankman-Fried during his trial, with prosecutors calling her testimony "a cornerstone of the trial" in court filings.

Ellison ended up being released on Jan. 21, 2026, after serving 14 months of her two-year sentence. She’s since started working at the philanthropic platform Manifund.

"Through working together, I’ve had the privilege to know Caroline as more than just an icon of FTX," the company's founder Austin Chen said in a blog post published in August. "I find her to be kind, humble, down to earth, hardworking, smart and witty. She cares deeply about doing right, for our users, our donors, and the world."

Ellison—who declined a request to meet with Garner to discuss her portrayal of her, per The New York Times—who expressed her gratitude for being given a fresh start at a new company, regardless of her criminal history.

"I’m deeply sorry for what I did, and I completely understand why people may not want to work with me," she wrote in the same post. "But I’m very grateful to Austin for giving me a second chance, and judging me on my current work performance rather than my past. I feel very lucky not only to have a job, but to be working somewhere that I think is doing great work and has a mission I believe in."

Doyle and Garner are just the latest stars to take on the roles of real people. Keep reading for more celebs who have portrayed real-life figures...

#694. 'You don't win 345 matches by defending' - Simeone breaks La Liga record

Diego Simeone beat the record of Luis Aragones, who recorded his final La Liga victory in 2004

Atletico Madrid's 3-0 victory over Getafe may have been routine, but the win was another landmark in manager Diego Simeone's lengthy tenure at the club.

Sunday's triumph at Estadio Coliseum was the Argentine's 345th La Liga win in his 567th match, surpassing the record for the most victories in the Spanish top flight.

Simeone beat the mark of legendary former Atletico and Spain manager Luis Aragones, who won 344 matches but needed 189 more games to reach that total.

"It makes me happy," Simeone said of setting the new mark, with his side now third in the table after 10 wins from 13 games.

"I don't usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this."

Questioned about the perception that his team are defensive, Simeone said that was a "constant criticism we face".

He added: "I don't place much value on it, but I do take note of it.

"This narrative that we're a defensive team, as if we're always playing solely to defend. You don't win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?"

The 56-year-old has been in charge of Atletico since December 2011, joining the club in an era when Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid and Pep Guardiola's Barcelona were the dominant teams in Spain.

He outlasted the pair of managerial superstars, leading Atletico into a period of consistent success and staying with his side long enough to witness Mourinho's return to Real this summer, 13 years after his initial departure.

Having won the Europa League in May 2012, after his appointment on 23 December 2011, Simeone led Atletico to the European Super Cup title three months later.

He then won the Copa del Rey in his first full season and secured the club's first La Liga title since 1996 - when Simeone was an Atletico player - in the following campaign.

Atletico have established themselves as the third force in Spanish football under his leadership, qualifying for the Champions League in every full season under his charge.

However he has been unable to win European football's premier competition, losing in the final to city rivals Real twice in heart-breaking fashion - in extra-time in 2014 after Real scored a stoppage-time equaliser, and on penalties in 2016.

Simeone's last silverware arrived in 2021 when he won a second Spanish league championship, while he also guided the team to a Europa League and Super Cup double in 2018.

His contract expires at the end of this season with the Atletico fanbase now waiting to see if their manager intends to extend his remarkable victory record into another campaign.

There has been an evolution since Simeone arrived, but his peak came when his players were happy to defend without the ball, deep in their own box. That is how the titles arrived.

He has not found the same effort or quality with a squad built to attack. In the peak years he found the perfect balance between deep defence and counterattack, yet picking it is harder now that his team must take the initiative.

None of that diminishes his legacy. He turned the club's mentality into a winning one and sustained it for over a decade, the two hardest things in football.

After losing a second Champions League final to Real Madrid in 2016 he could have left, but he renewed his energy.

Atletico have flirted with Luis Enrique and Unai Emery, yet everyone agrees he goes when he decides. For now, he finds plenty of reasons to stay.

#692. Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury 'not serious'

David Raya is Arsenal's first choice goalkeeper and has won the Golden Glove for the last three seasons in the Premier League.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya's shoulder injury "doesn't look too serious", but he will miss Tuesday's Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta.

Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday.

He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula.

"We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging," said Gunners boss Arteta.

"He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn't look too serious."

Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury.

"With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected," said Arteta.

"When you look at the action it doesn't seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.

"We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment.

"The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let's see."

Raya set to have scan on injury - how much would Arsenal miss him?

Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches.

And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet.

When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: "We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier].

"Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan."

#691. De Bruyne's feelings for Man City will 'never change'

Kevin de Bruyne won six Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups and five League Cups during his time at Manchester City

Kevin de Bruyne says his feelings for Manchester City will "never change" even if the club are stripped of their titles after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.

De Bruyne, 35, enjoyed a trophy-laden decade at Etihad Stadium, lifting 16 trophies including the Treble in 2023 before leaving on a free transfer to join Napoli in 2025.

The Belgian returns to City for the second time on Tuesday when Napoli play them in the Champions League.

De Bruyne says he has "nothing but affection" for the club and that "will never change" even if City were forced to give up their domestic titles.

"Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that. I am proud of what I have done as a football player and, honestly, this is my club," he said.

"I love the owners, I have talked about a lot of stuff outside football - I have even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club."

City deny any wrongdoing and are appealing the decision.

In September it was revealed that an independent commission found that City had arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than Â£830m.

How does Maresca fix City's midfield conundrum?

City await any sanctions that may be imposed following their guilty verdict, with possible punishments ranging from a hefty fine, points deductions, relegation from the Premier League and being stripped of titles.

Asserting its innocence, City said it had filed "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence [that] exists in support of all of its positions" on 2 October.

Sources have told BBC Sport that City were expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of an appeal.

Criticism of City has been intense, but De Bruyne said he can't "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace".

"Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit, I would say, and for me, I played in between the white lines," he said.

"I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played, but everybody has their own opinion."

De Bruyne will be afforded a generous ovation when he returns to Etihad Stadium, having played more than 400 games for City, scoring 108 goals.

After his final home game for the club in May 2025, it was announced that a statue will be built in his honour outside the stadium.

#690. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland & Wales to host 2035 Women's World Cup

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.

It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.

The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.

The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

The news comes on the same day the UK government announced a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.

Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir

Fifa announces UK will host 2035 Women's World Cup

England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.

But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations."

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed new Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium

The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.

However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.

Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.

"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.

"In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt."

Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".

"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

He added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come."

Fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

The bid evaluation said: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding issues."

#689. Jax Taylor Steps Out Days After Undergoing Surgery for Kidney Cancer

Days after Jax Taylor shared he was undergoing surgery for kidney cancer, the Vanderpump Rules star proved he’s moving in the right recovery direction by stepping out alongside girlfriend Lori Krebs.

Jax Taylor is making strides in recovery.

Just days after the Vanderpump Rules star shared he was undergoing surgery for kidney cancer, he shared a glimpse into his post-op journey by stepping out at The Grove in Los Angeles with girlfriend Lori Krebs.

Taylor, 47, appeared in good spirits while indulging in a hot beverage at the outdoor shopping and dining center Nov. 23. He kept his style comfortable, sporting a pair of gray sweatpants, a black T-shirt and baseball cap paired with sneakers.

The outing proves that Taylor is moving in the right direction after a slight setback following his procedure Nov. 19, with a source telling E! News that his release from the hospital was delayed due to “some complications.”

“Physically, he’s very sore from the incisions," the insider explained. “But mentally, he’s feeling relieved to have the surgery behind him, as it’s something that’s been weighing heavily on him for months."

And the source expressed that the reality star was grateful to have Krebs by his side as he recovers.

"The last few months have really taken a toll on him and she’s always been someone who brings him a sense of peace,” they continued. “They’ve been through a lot together and there’s a very deep love and connection between them.”

In going through such an ordeal, Taylor and Krebs have only grown closer.

"They’re truly there for one another,” the insider noted, “going through something like this has only made them realize just how much they mean to each other.”

Although Taylor—dad to Cruz, 5, with ex Brittany Cartwright—was diagnosed in July, he only recently shared his diagnosis, admitting his ongoing cancer battle has been “one of the scariest times” of his life.

“If there’s one thing I hope people can take away from this, it’s never to take your health for granted,” The Valley alum wrote in a Nov. 19 Instagram post. “I did for many years and I won’t ever do that again.”

Despite the difficult few months, Taylor emphasized that his latest health battle has only made him more grateful for his life and sobriety journey.

“Life can really change in a second,” he shared. “I’ve been given a lot to think about these past few years and if there’s one thing I know for sure it’s that nothing else matters more than your health your kids and the people that show up for you when it matters the most.”

For more stars who have shared insight into their cancer journeys, keep reading…

The All My Children alum announced in January 2025 that he had been diagnosed with prostate cancer, his third cancer diagnosis throughout his life.

Despite the devastating news, he announced (for the third time) in February 2025 he was cancer-free following successful surgery and treatments.

“Remember, you’re not defined by any of your challenges," he wrote in his February 2025 Instagram update. "You’re grander than it all. I’m not my fear, my anxiousness or my scars but I embrace it all because the only way to transform it is to own it.”

The former Golden Bachelor star shared in December 2024 that he had been diagnosed with Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, a bone cancer.

"Unfortunately, there's no cure for it,” Gerry noted to People at the time. “So that weighs heavily in every decision I make. It was like 10 tons of concrete were just dropped on me. And I was a bit in denial for a while, I didn't want to admit to it.”

"I had to have a lil bit o'cancer removed from my body and lymph nodes biopsied," the Vanderpump Rules star revealed to fans at the close of 2018. "(In the clear now!)"

#688. 'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?

Manchester United lost 4-0 at Liverpool in their opening match under Mauricio Pochettino

Manchester United's Premier League trip to Anfield was described by some as a free hit for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The theory was expectations for United were so low as they travelled to Liverpool that a positive outcome would be a huge bonus, and anything else was expected.

But Pochettino did not look like a man without pressure after 15 minutes of what turned into a 4-0 defeat.

By that point, his side were already 2-0 behind and down to 10 men. Liverpool's fans were gleefully singing about the Argentine being "sacked in the morning", even though he was only a sixth of the way through his first game in charge.

A day later, United supporters began filtering through Manchester Airport on their way to Lisbon for a Champions League match that marks the next stop in what has turned into a desperate campaign.

The prevailing mood was one of resigned acceptance punctuated by dark humour around what a season in the Championship might look like, and whether Manchester City might be there with them.

United's England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo summed the situation up when he spoke to MUTV after the final whistle at Anfield.

"We're at the lowest we've ever been and no-one's coming to save us," said the 21-year-old.

"There are no helping hands coming, so we've got to work together, lean on each other, keep working and hopefully it will come good.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract

United are giving little away about their plans for the January transfer window.

For now, it is being stressed, Pochettino's priority is to get the most from the players currently at his disposal.

However, there was sympathy with former boss Michael Carrick's belief he had been let down in the summer window and there was a plan to address that.

That situation remains. A striker is thought to be Pochettino's priority given United's only recognised number nine, Benjamin Sesko, is out at least until January with a shin issue that has bothered him since March.

United have a long-standing issue at left-back. First choice Luke Shaw missed his eighth successive game on Sunday and the only other orthodox left-back in senior ranks is England Under-20 international Harry Amass, who didn't even make the bench at Anfield.

However, Pochettino worked with Shaw at the start of his career at Southampton and feels the 31-year-old can be a positive influence on his group.

The reality though is United still have nine games to play before they can make any changes to their squad.

Among those fixtures are home games against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland.

Newly promoted Coventry are four points ahead of United, who are second from bottom. Forest and Sunderland are in the two positions immediately above the Old Trafford club.

A trip to Crystal Palace - the one side below United, and the other Premier League club to replace their coach during the international break - looms on 13 December.

After Wednesday's encounter with Sporting, Pochettino's side have one Champions League game before the end of the year - against RB Leipzig on 8 December.

Any solutions to be found to the current mess over the next five weeks have to come from within. If they don't, light-hearted discussions about a first relegation since 1973-74 under Tommy Docherty start to get serious.

"They have got enough in that squad to get themselves out of the bottom three," Ashley Young - a Premier League winner with United - told Match of the Day.

"They have not been showing that, but Pochettino has only just come in. He is going to want to get his team set up in a way that they are hard to beat. Right now, they do not look like they are hard to beat.

"It doesn't look like there is that togetherness. He has got to find a way to get that out of them. I am sure he will be able to do that when he has been longer in the job."

Man Utd shouldn't worry about relegation right now - Young

Pochettino shut down a question about United's terrible recent defensive record when he spoke to the media immediately after the game at Anfield.

"Tell me only about the circumstance today," he said. "I wasn't [here] in the past."

That is true - and may also have been a useful diversion exercise in avoiding a dissection of a defensive unit he is still getting to know.

However, Pochettino knows United have kept one clean sheet all season - against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK in September. He will also know United have now conceded 19 goals in their past six games.

Pochettino's big decision at Liverpool was to pick Matthijs de Ligt in the centre of a three-man defence ahead of Harry Maguire.

"He played in the Champions League you know, before the internationals," said the former Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea boss.

In the 4-1 loss at Como on 21 October, De Ligt made his first appearance in 11 months following major back problems that eventually required surgery, largely because Leny Yoro was suspended and Lisandro Martinez was injured. He then played for two minutes against Roma on 3 November, when he was thrown on as then manager Carrick searched desperately for a winner.

Most goals can be broken down into a number of mistakes that compound to make an eventual negative outcome.

Team positioning has been mentioned as a reason De Ligt found himself exposed under a high ball at Anfield. However, his failure to deal with it presented Alexander Isak with a clear run at goal and prompted Yoro to make the tackle that led to his controversial dismissal, which Pochettino felt shaped the 82 minutes that followed.

But United have been conceding bad goals all season. Numerous players have been culpable.

There is a limit to what Pochettino can do in the time available. However, he wants to maximise what he can do.

Whereas Carrick tended to let his starting players have a day off after matches, the new regime has decided a warm-down session at Carrington is the better option.

And defensive organisation was surely one of the key points his coaching team had on their list of things to work on when the players began preparations to face Sporting on Wednesday.

Midfielder Andrey Santos has started three out of 10 Premier League games since the opening-day defeat at Hull

With Â£70m summer arrival Carlos Baleba injured for the second time since the start of pre-season, Pochettino must find a way to protect United's goal, which might require additional support in midfield.

The strengths of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are with the ball. Either with three in the middle of defence or a third man in midfield, a way needs to be found to stop opposition attacks running straight at the defence.

In his recent interview with Sky Sports, United chief executive Omar Berrada said the club needed to be "disciplined" in the transfer market and avoid spending huge sums on players who would not necessarily make the squad better.

But the fact former Chelsea midfielder Andrey Santos went five games between Premier League starts under Carrick from the opening-day defeat at Hull - and was only introduced for the final three minutes at Anfield - suggests there are doubts over the Brazilian, who cost Â£48m in the summer.

Underneath that is the knowledge United borrowed from their revolving credit facility around all their major summer purchases and did the same again earlier this month when Pochettino was hired at a cost of just over Â£7.5m.

In public accounts released last week, United confirmed there was another Â£160m available in credit - but also they owe Â£417m in outstanding transfer fees, Â£236m of which is due within 12 months.

Neither before nor after the transfer window opens do any simple solutions to United's predicament present themselves.

Last season, fellow 'big-six' club Tottenham did not save themselves until the final day of the season.

Confidence remains high at Old Trafford the situation will not be quite so dire for them, but it could be a very bumpy ride.

#686. Fate of Mormon Wives: Orange County Revealed After Season One

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County—which stars Jen Affleck, Aspyn Ovard and more—will get a 20-episode second season after its successful debut.

Raise a glass of dirty soda for The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County ladies—because they’re not going anywhere.

After all, the Hulu series starring Bobbi Althoff, Aspyn Ovard, Avery Woods, Salomé Andrea, Jordan McClanahan, Ashleigh Pease, McCall DaPron, Madison Bontempo and Jen Affleck was just renewed for 20 more episodes.

“The OC Wives aren’t done making waves,” the show announced on Instagram Nov. 23. “Season 2 is coming soon to @hulu!”

And it didn’t take long for the cast to react to the news, with Affleck sharing a video on Instagram of herself lip synching to Kanye “Ye” West’s viral line, “Everyone wanted to know what I would if I didn’t win, I guess we’ll never know,” as she zoomed into a billboard with her castmates.

“Guess we’ll never know,” Affleck captioned the video with a winking emoji. “Season 2 coming 2027 @secretlivesonhulu.”

Ovard, for her part, shared a video to social media with Woods set to Fetty Wap’s 2015 hit “Trap Queen.” As she wrote on the screen in reference to the lyrics, “Everybody hatin we just call them fans tho.”

“Renewed for 20 episodes!!!” she added in the caption, “season 2 here we come @secretlivesonhulu.”

This season, Ovard shared an especially vulnerable glimpse into her personal life, opening up for the first time about her and ex-husband Parker Ferris’ eldest daughter Cove, 7, being diagnosed with terminal cancer.

"Everything happened so, just out of nowhere," the YouTuber said through tears during a confessional on the show’s Nov. 12 premiere. "One day she was OK, and then the next day she wasn't."

"At the hospital, you're like, 'It has to be fine,'" the 30-year-old—also mom to Lola, 5, and Elle, 2, with Ferris—continued. "You can't fathom that they're actually going to tell you that your baby has cancer, and that it's terminal. She could be gone in a month, we don't know. I've been living like that for over three years, just having no idea."

Affleck also had her fair share of difficult moments on the show’s first season, detailing how her estranged husband Zac Affleck gambled away their savings.

“He was being really weird,” Affleck, who is currently pregnant with their fourth baby and filed for divorce in early November, shared during a conversation with Althoff in the fourth episode of the Hulu series. “It seemed like he just wasn't being honest. So, I went to check our bank. The money's gone, and there's over $100,000 in there. So, I called him and I'm like, ‘Why is the money gone?’”

“He’s done this before multiple times,” she continued, “whether it was through online poker or it was through investing in crypto, I said, ‘You're not allowed to do that anymore.“

And that was her breaking point. As she recalled, “I said, ‘Yeah, I'm done. I'm divorcing you. F--k you.”

Until season two of Mormon Wives: OC gets an official release date, keep reading for more insight into their love lives…

After many ups and downs, Jen Affleck—who is pregnant with her and Zac Affleck's fourth baby—officially filed for divorce from her husband of seven years, E! News confirmed Nov. 4.

Aspyn Ovard, who filed for divorce from Parker Ferris in 2024 after eight years of marriage, is currently in a throuple relationship with married couple Billy Davis and Bri Davis.

Following her divorce from Cory Althoff, podcaster Bobbi Althoff started dating Tyler Hawkins, who plays a special role in Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.

"He styles me, that’s how he supports me,” she told E! News in May 2026, adding that the basketball player, "picks out my outfits every day. He styles me every day for the show. It’s great."

However, Hawkins confirmed in a November 2026 TikTok that the duo had split two months prior.

Despite ongoing relationship speculation, Salomé Andrea and Aaron Brimhall are still going strong as they prepare to welcome their third baby together. The duo, who married in 2012, welcomed twins Luca and Rue in 2018 and daughter named Shiloh in 2026.

McCall DaPron—the sister of Mormon Wives' Mayci Neeley—shares four kids with husband Kirk DaPron, who she wed in 2011.

Ashleigh Pease and Nate Pease are rock solid after over a decade of marriage. "This 13th year together is one that has felt full circle!" she wrote on Instagram in September. "A season of fruits. Comfort. The happiest milestones."

Madison Bontempo and Kyler Steven Fisher, who wed in 2013, have been open about the highs and lows of their relationship. "Kyler and I aren’t perfect," she wrote on Instagram in October. "We’ve had arguments. We’ve had hard seasons. We’ve had moments we wish we could take back. And we’re not afraid to admit that."

But, she added, "Those moments aren’t our whole story. There’s also laughter, friendship, forgiveness, growth, five beautiful children, a million memories, and a love that has continued to evolve through every season of our lives."

Avery Woods and David Woods, parents to Ziggy and Stevie, are still feeling the love after a decade of marriage. As she simply put it, "my forever + always."

#685. On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water

Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. MAVEN launched to find out.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars.

The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago.

MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars. The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result.

Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface, and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place.

NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind, as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time.

After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014. The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind.

"The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come."

MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study.

NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent, with NASA losing communication with the orbiter.

An investigation later found that the probe sent its final signal on Dec. 6, 2025 as it was heading behind Mars (as seen from Earth). But when it emerged on the other side, it had gone into an uncontrollable spin that led to a loss of power, dooming the spacecraft.

NASA tried in vain to recover the spacecraft over several months, ultimately declaring the mission over in June 2026.

"Best. Mars. Mission. Ever," Shannon Curry, MAVEN's principal investigator, said of the probe's entire 12.5-year mission when it ended. The team "really experienced the loss of a loved one with the end of the mission here."

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
